de.7:143: Auch als Moses zu Unserem Termin gekommen war und sein Herr zu ihm gesprochen hatte, sagte er: "Mein Herr, zeige (Dich) mir, auf daß ich Dich schauen mag." Er sprach: "Du wirst Mich nicht sehen, doch blicke auf den Berg; wenn er unverrückt an seinem Ort bleibt, dann wirst du Mich sehen." Als nun sein Herr dem Berg erschien, da ließ Er ihn zu Schutt zerfallen, und Moses stürzte ohnmächtig nieder. Und als er zu sich kam, sagte er: "Gepriesen seist Du, ich bekehre mich zu Dir, und ich bin der Erste der Glaubende."
de.7:144: Er sprach: "O Moses, Ich habe dich vor den Menschen durch Meine Botschaft und durch Mein Wort zu dir auserwählt. So nimm denn hin, was Ich dir gegeben habe, und sei einer der Dankbaren."
de.7:145: Auch Wir schrieben ihm auf den Tafeln allerlei auf zur Ermahnung und Erklärung von allen Dingen: "So halte sie fest und befiehl deinem Volk, das Beste davon zu befolgen". Bald werde Ich euch die Stätte der Übeltäter sehen lassen.
de.7:146: Abwenden aber will Ich von Meinen Zeichen diejenigen, die sich im Lande hochmütig gegen alles Recht gebärden; und wenn sie auch alle Zeichen sehen, so wollen sie nicht daran glauben; und wenn sie den Weg der Rechtschaffenheit sehen, so wollen sie ihn nicht als Weg annehmen; sehen sie aber den Weg des Irrtums, so nehmen sie ihn als Weg an. Dies (ist so), weil sie Unsere Zeichen für Lügen erklärten und sie nicht achteten.
de.7:147: Diejenigen, die Unsere Zeichen und ihre Begegnung im Jenseits leugnen - deren Werke sind hinfällig. Können sie für etwas anderes als das, was sie getan haben, belohnt werden?
de.7:148: Auch die Leute Moses' nahmen sich, nachdem er weggegangen war, aus ihren Schmucksachen ein leibhaftiges Kalb, das muhte. Sahen sie denn nicht, daß es nicht zu ihnen sprechen und sie nicht auf den rechten Weg führen könnte? Sie nahmen es sich, und sie wurden Übeltäter.
de.7:149: Als sie dann von Reue erfaßt wurden und einsahen, daß sie wirklich irregegangen waren, da sagten sie: "Wenn Sich unser Herr nicht unser erbarmt und uns verzeiht, so werden wir ganz gewiß unter den Verlierenden sein."
de.7:150: Auch als Moses zu seinen Leuten zurückkehrte, zornig und voller Gram, da sagte er: "Es ist schlimm, was ihr in meiner Abwesenheit an meiner Stelle verübt habt. Wolltet ihr den Befehl eures Herrn beschleunigen?" Und er warf die Tafeln hin und packte seinen Bruder beim Kopf und zerrte ihn zu sich. Er (Aaron) sagte: "Sohn meiner Mutter, siehe, das Volk hielt mich für schwach, und fast hätten sie mich getötet. Darum laß die Feinde nicht über mich frohlocken und weise mich nicht dem Volk der Ungerechten zu."
de.7:151: Er (Moses) sagte: "Mein Herr, vergib mir und meinem Bruder und gewähre uns Zutritt zu Deiner Barmherzig keit; denn Du bist der Barmherzigste der Allerbarmende."
de.7:152: Fürwahr, diejenigen, die sich nun das Kalb nahmen, wird der Zorn ihres Herrn sowie Schmach im diesseitigen Leben treffen. Und so belohnen Wir diejenigen, die Lügen erdichten.
de.7:153: Diejenigen aber, die Böses taten und es dann bereuten und glaubten - fürwahr, dein Herr ist hernach Allverzeihend, Barmherzig.
de.7:154: Auch als der Zorn von Moses abließ, nahm er die Tafeln, und in ihrer Niederschrift war Rechtleitung und Barmherzigkeit für jene, die ihren Herrn fürchten.
de.7:155: Auch Moses erwählte aus seinem Volk siebzig Männer für Unsere Verabredung. Doch als das Beben sie ereilte, sagte er: "Mein Herr, hättest Du es gewollt, hättest Du sie zuvor vernichten können und mich ebenfalls. Willst Du uns denn vernichten um dessentwillen, was die Toren unter uns getan haben? Dies ist nur eine Prüfung von Dir. Damit führst Du irre, wen Du willst, und weist den Weg, wem Du willst. Du bist unser Beschützer; so vergib uns denn und erbarme Dich unser; denn Du bist der Beste der Vergebenden.
de.7:156: Auch bestimme für uns Gutes, sowohl im Diesseits als auch im Jenseits; denn zu Dir sind wir reuevoll zurückgekehrt." Er sprach: "Ich treffe mit Meiner Strafe, wen Ich will; doch Meine Barmherzigkeit umfaßt alle Dinge; so werde Ich sie bestimmen - sowohl für jene, die (Mich) fürchten und die Zakah entrichten als auch für jene, die an Unsere Zeichen glauben."
de.7:157: Dies sind jene, die dem Botschaftern, dem Propheten folgen, der des Lesens und Schreibens unkundig ist; dort in der Thora und im Evangelium werden sie über ihn (geschrieben) finden: er gebietet ihnen das Gute und verbietet ihnen das Böse, und er erlaubt ihnen die guten Dinge und verwehrt ihnen die schlechten, und er nimmt ihnen ihre Last hinweg und die Fesseln, die auf ihnen lagen -; die also an ihn glauben und ihn stärken und ihm helfen und dem Licht folgen, das mit ihm hinabgesandt wurde, die sollen erfolgreich sein.
de.7:158: Sprich: "O ihr Menschen, ich bin für euch alle ein Botschafter Allahs, Dessen das Königreich der Himmel und der Erde ist. Es ist kein Allah außer Ihm. Er macht lebendig und läßt sterben. Darum glaubt an Allah und an Seinen Botschaftern, den Propheten, der des Lesens und Schreibens unkundig ist, der an Allah und an Seine Worte glaubt; und folgt ihm, auf daß ihr rechtgeleitet werden möget."
de.7:159: Auch unter dem Volke Moses' gibt es eine Gemeinde, die in Wahrheit den Weg weist und danach Gerechtigkeit übt.
de.7:160: Auch Wir teilten sie in zwölf Stämme zu Gemeinschaften auf, und Wir offenbarten Moses, als sein Volk von ihm etwas zu trinken forderte: "Schlage mit " deinem Stock an den Felsen." Da entsprangen ihm zwölf Quellen: so kannte jeder Stamm seinen Trinkplatz. Und Wir ließen sie von Wolken überschatten und sandten ihnen Manna und Salwa hinab: "Esset von den guten Dingen, die Wir euch beschert haben." Und sie schädigten nicht Uns, sondern sich selbst haben sie Schaden zugefügt.
de.7:161: Auch wenn ihnen gesagt wird: "Wohnt in dieser Stadt und nehmet von ihr eure Speise, wo immer ihr wollt, und sprecht: "Vergebung!" und geht durch das Tor ein, indem ihr euch niederwerft! Dann werden Wir euch eure Sünden vergeben; fürwahr, Wir werden jenen, die Gutes tun, noch mehr (an Gnade) erweisen."
de.7:162: Da vertauschten die Ungerechten unter ihnen den Ausspruch mit einem anderen als dem, der zu ihnen gesprochen worden war. Darum sandten Wir wegen ihres frevelhaften Tuns ein Strafgericht vom Himmel über sie hernieder.
de.7:163: Auch frage sie nach der Stadt, die am Meer lag, und (danach,) wie sie den Sabbat entweihten, wie ihre Fische scharenweise an ihrem Sabbattage zu ihnen kamen. Doch an dem Tage, da sie den Sabbat nicht feierten, da kamen sie nicht zu ihnen. So prüften Wir sie, weil sie gefrevelt hatten.
de.7:164: Auch als eine Gemeinschaft unter ihnen sagte: "Warum ermahnt ihr Leute, die Allah vernichten oder mit einer strengen Strafe bestrafen will?" - da sagten sie (die Ermahner): "Zur Entschuldigung vor eurem Herrn, und damit sie gottesfürchtig werden mögen."
de.7:165: Auch als sie das vergaßen, womit sie ermahnt worden waren, da retteten Wir jene, die das Böse verhindert hatten, und erfaßten die Ungerechten mit peinlicher Strafe, weil sie gefrevelt hatten.
de.7:166: Auch als sie trotzig bei dem verharrten, was ihnen verboten worden war, da sprachen Wir zu ihnen: "Werdet denn verächtliche Affen! "
de.7:167: Auch (gedenke der Zeit,) da dein Herr verkündete, Er wolle gewiß gegen sie bis zum Tage der Auferstehung solche entsenden, die sie mit grimmiger Pein bedrängen würden. Fürwahr, dein Herr ist schnell im Strafen. Und fürwahr, Er ist Allvergebend, Barmherzig.
de.7:168: Auch Wir haben sie auf Erden in Gemeinschaften zerteilt. Unter ihnen sind Tugendhafte, und unter ihnen gibt es welche, die nicht so sind. Und Wir prüften sie durch Gutes und durch Böses, auf daß sie sich bekehren mögen.
de.7:169: Es folgten ihnen dann Nachkommen, die die Offenbarungsschrift erbten; sie greifen aber nach den armseligen Gütern dieser niedrigen (Welt) und sagen: "Es wird uns verziehen werden." Doch wenn (abermals) derartige Güter zu ihnen kämen, griffen sie wiederum danach. Wurde denn der Bund der Offenbarungsschrift nicht mit ihnen geschlossen, damit sie von Allah nichts als die Wahrheit aussagen sollten? Und sie haben gelesen, was darin steht. Aber die Wohnstätte im Jenseits ist besser für die Gottesfürchtigen. Wollt ihr es denn nicht begreifen?
de.7:170: Auch diejenigen, die an der Offenbarungsschrift festhalten und die Gebete darbringen Wir lassen den Tugendhafte den Lohn nicht verlorengehen.
de.7:171: Auch da Wir den Berg über ihnen schüttelten, als wäre er ein Schattenspender, und sie dachten, er würde auf sie stürzen (, da sprachen Wir): " Haltet fest, was Wir euch gegeben haben, und denkt daran, was darin steht, auf daß ihr gottesfürchtig werden möget."
de.7:172: Auch als dein Herr aus den Kindern Adams - aus ihren Lenden ihre Nachkommenschaft hervorbrachte und sie zu Zeugen gegen Sich Selbst machte (, indem Er sprach): "Bin Ich nicht euer Herr?", sagten sie: "Doch, wir bezeugen es." (Dies ist so,) damit ihr nicht am Tage der Auferstehung sprecht: "Siehe, wir wußten nichts davon."
de.7:173: Oder (damit ihr nicht) sprecht: "Es waren bloß unsere Väter, die vordem Götzendiener waren; wir aber waren ein Geschlecht nach ihnen. Willst Du uns denn vernichten um dessentwillen, was die Verlogenen taten?"
de.7:174: Auch so machen Wir die Zeichen klar, auf daß sie sich bekehren mögen.
de.7:175: Auch erzähle ihnen die Geschichte dessen, dem Wir Unsere Zeichen gaben, der aber an ihnen vorbeiglitt; so folgte der Widersacher ihm nach, und er wurde einer der Irregegangenen.
de.7:176: Auch hätten Wir es gewollt, hätten Wir ihn dadurch erhöhen können; doch er neigte der Erde zu und folgte seiner eigenen Neigung. Er gleicht daher einem Hunde: treibst du ihn fort, so hängt er seine Zunge heraus; läßt du aber von ihm ab, so hängt er auch seine Zunge heraus. Gerade so ergeht es Leuten, die Unsere Zeichen leugnen. Darum erzähle (ihnen) die Geschichten, auf daß sie sich besinnen mögen.
de.7:177: Schlimm ist das Beispiel der Leute, die Unsere Zeichen leugnen und gegen sich selbst gesündigt haben.
de.7:178: Derjenige, den Allah rechtleitet, ist auf dem rechten Weg. Diejenigen aber, die Er irreführt, sind fürwahr jene, die verloren haben.
de.7:179: Wir haben viele Ginn und Menschen erschaffen, deren Ende Gahannam sein wird! Sie haben Herzen, mit denen sie nicht begreifen, und sie haben Augen, mit denen sie nicht sehen, und sie haben Ohren, mit denen sie nicht hören; sie sind wie das Vieh; nein, sie irren noch eher (vom Weg) ab. Sie sind fürwahr unbedacht.
de.7:180: Auch Allahs sind die Schönsten Namen; so ruft Ihn mit ihnen an. Und lasset jene sein, die hinsichtlich Seiner Namen eine abwegige Haltung einnehmen. Ihnen wird das vergolten werden, was sie getan haben.
de.7:181: Auch unter denen, die Wir erschufen, gibt es eine Gemeinschaft, die mit der Wahrheit leitet und danach Gerechtigkeit übt.
de.7:182: Diejenigen aber, die Unsere Zeichen leugnen, werden Wir Schritt für Schritt erniedrigen, ohne daß sie begreifen, wie dies geschah.
de.7:183: Auch Ich werde ihnen Aufschub gewähren; denn fürwahr, Meine Pläne sind stark angelegt.
de.7:184: Haben sie denn nicht darüber nachgedacht, daß ihr Gefährte nicht besessen ist? Er ist nichts anderes als ein deutlicher Warner.
de.7:185: Haben sie denn nicht das Reich der Himmel und der Erde betrachtet und alle Dinge, die Allah geschaffen hat, und (haben sie nicht bedacht,) daß sich ihre Lebensfrist vielleicht schon dem Ende nähert? Woran sonst wollen sie wohl nach dieser Verkündigung glauben?
de.7:186: Für den, den Allah irreführt, kann es keinen geben, der ihn rechtleitet; und Er läßt sie in ihrer Widerspenstigkeit blindlings umherirren.
de.7:187: Sie befragen dich nach der Stunde, wann sie wohl eintreten werde. Sprich: "Das Wissen darum ist bei meinem Herrn. Keiner als Er kann sie (die Stunde) zu ihrer Zeit bekannt geben. Schwer lastet sie in den Himmeln und auf der Erde. Sie soll über euch nur plötzlich hereinbrechen." Sie befragen dich, als ob du von ihr genaue Kenntnis besäßest. Sprich: "Das Wissen darum ist bei meinem Herrn; doch die meisten Menschen wissen es nicht."
de.7:188: Sprich: "Ich habe nicht die Macht, mir selbst zu nützen oder zu schaden, es sei denn, Allah will es. Und hätte ich Kenntnis von dem Verborgenen, fürwahr, ich hätte mir die Fülle des Guten zu sichern vermocht, und Übeles hätte mich nicht berührt. Ich bin ja nur ein Warner und ein Bringer froher Botschaft für die Leute, die gläubig sind."
de.7:189: Er ist es, Der euch aus einer einzigen Seele erschuf; und aus ihm machte Er seine Gattin, damit er bei ihr ruhe. Als er ihr dann beigewohnt hatte, war sie mit einer leichten Last schwanger und ging mit ihr umher. Und wenn sie schwer wird, dann beten beide zu Allah, ihrem Herrn: "Wenn Du uns ein gutes (Kind) gibst, so werden wir fürwahr unter den Dankbaren sein."
de.7:190: Doch wenn Er ihnen dann ein gutes (Kind) gibt, so schreiben sie Seine ihnen gewahrte Gabe Göttern zu. Aber Allah ist über alles Erhaben, was sie (Ihm) zur Seite stellen.
de.7:191: Wollen sie denn jene Teilhaber (anbeten), die nichts erschaffen können und selbst (nur) Erschaffene sind?
de.7:192: Auch sie vermögen ihnen keine Hilfe zu gewähren, noch können sie sich selber helfen.
de.7:193: Auch wenn ihr sie zum rechten Weg ruft, dann folgen sie euch nicht. Es ist ganz gleich für euch, ob ihr sie ruft oder ob ihr schweigt.
de.7:194: Jene, die ihr statt Allah ruft, sind selbst erschaffene (Wesen) wie ihr. Ruft sie denn an und lasset sie euch Antwort geben, wenn ihr wahrhaftig seid.
de.7:195: Haben sie etwa Füße, um zu gehen, oder haben sie Hände, um zu greifen, oder haben sie Augen, um zu sehen, oder haben sie Ohren, um zu hören? Sprich: "Ruft eure Götter an; dann schmiedet Listen gegen mich und lasset mich nicht lange warten.
de.7:196: Fürwahr, mein Beschützer ist Allah, Der die Heilige Schrift herabgesandt hat. Und Er beschützt die Tugendhafte.
de.7:197: Die aber, die ihr statt Ihm anruft, vermögen euch nicht zu helfen, noch können sie sich selber helfen."
de.7:198: Auch wenn ihr sie zum rechten Weg ruft, so hören sie (euch) nicht. Und du siehst sie nach dir schauen, doch sie sehen nicht.
de.7:199: sbe Nachsicht, gebiete das Rechte und wende dich von den Unwissenden ab.
de.7:200: Auch wenn du zu einer bösen Tat vom der Widersacher aufgestachelt worden bist, dann nimm deine Zuflucht bei Allah; fürwahr, Er ist Allhörend, Allwissend.
de.7:201: Fürwahr, diejenigen, die dann gottesfürchtig sind, wenn sie eine Heimsuchung durch der Widersacher trifft, und sich dann ermahnen lassen: siehe, gleich sehen sie (ihren klaren Weg) wieder.
de.7:202: Aber ihre (heidnischen) Brüder treiben sie dazu, im Irrtum fortzufahren, und dann lassen sie (darin) nicht nach.
de.7:203: Wenn du ihnen kein Zeichen bringst, sagen sie: "Warum erfindest du es nicht?" Sprich: "Ich folge nur dem, was mir von meinem Herrn offenbart wurde. Dies sind sichtbare Beweise von eurem Herrn und eine Führung und Barmherzigkeit für gläubige Leute."
de.7:204: Auch wenn der Quran verlesen wird, so hört zu und schweigt in Aufmerksamkeit, auf daß ihr Erbarmen finden möget.
de.7:205: Auch gedenke deines Herrn in deinem Herzen in Demut und Furcht, ohne laut vernehmbare Worte am Morgen und am Abend; und sei nicht einer der Unachtsamen.
de.7:206: Fürwahr, diejenigen, die bei deinem Herrn sind, sind nicht zu hochmütig dazu, Ihm zu dienen; sie lobpreisen Ihn und werfen sich vor Ihm nieder.
de.70:1: Ein Fragender fragt nach einer Strafe, die hereinbrechen wird
de.70:2: die für die Gottesleugner unabwendbar ist
de.70:3: sie ist von Allah, Der über die Himmelsleiter verfügt.
de.70:4: Die Gottesboten und Gabriel steigen zu Ihm auf in einem Tage, dessen Ausmaß fünfzigtausend Jahre beträgt.
de.70:7: aber Wir sehen, er ist nahe.
de.70:8: Am Tage, da der Himmel wie geschmolzenes Metall sein wird
de.70:9: und die Berge wie farbige Wollflocken
de.70:10: und ein Freund nicht mehr nach einem Freunde fragen wird
de.70:11: werden sie in Sichtweite zueinander gebracht werden, und der Schuldige würde sich wohl (gern) loskaufen von der Strafe jenes Tages mit seinen Kindern
de.70:12: und seiner Frau und seinem Bruder
de.70:13: und seiner Verwandtschaft, die ihn beherbergt hat
de.70:14: und allen, die insgesamt auf Erden sind, wenn es ihn nur retten könnte.
de.70:15: Nein! Es ist fürwahr eine Feuerflamme
de.70:17: Den wird sie rufen, der (Mir) den Rücken kehrt und sich (von Mir) abwendet
de.70:19: Fürwahr, der Mensch ist (seiner Natur nach) kleinmütig geschaffen worden.
de.70:20: Wenn ihn ein Unheil trifft, so gerät er in große Panik
de.70:21: doch wenn ihm (etwas) Gutes zukommt, ist er geizig.
de.70:22: Nicht so sind diejenigen, die beten
de.70:24: und die, in deren Besitztum ein bestimmter Anteil ist
de.70:25: für den Bittenden und den Unbemittelten
de.70:26: und die, die an den Tag des Gerichts glauben
de.70:27: und die, die vor der Strafe ihres Herrn besorgt sind
de.70:28: - fürwahr die Strafe ihres Herrn ist nichts, wovor man sicher sein könnte -
de.70:29: und die, die ihre Scham bewahren
de.70:30: außer bei ihren Gattinnen oder denen, die sie von Rechts wegen besitzen; denn da sind sie nicht zu tadeln.
de.70:31: Diejenigen aber, die darüber hinaus etwas suchen, das sind die Übertreter.
de.70:32: Auch die, die mit dem ihnen anvertrauten Gut redlich umgehen und erfüllen, wozu sie sich verpflichtet haben
de.70:33: und die, die in ihrer Zeugenaussage aufrichtig sind
de.70:34: und die, die ihr Gebet getreulich verrichten
de.70:35: diese sind es, die in den Gärten hochgeehrt sein werden.
de.70:36: Was aber ist mit denen, die ungläubig sind, daß sie auf dich zugelaufen kommen
de.70:37: von rechts und links, nach Gruppen plaziert?
de.70:38: Hofft jeder einzelne von ihnen wohl, den Garten der Wonne zu betreten?
de.70:39: Nimmermehr! Sie wissen doch, woraus Wir sie erschufen.
de.70:40: Aber nein! Ich schwöre beim Herrn der Aufgänge und der Untergänge, daß Wir imstande sind
de.70:41: bessere als sie an ihre Stelle zu setzen, und keiner kann Uns (daran) hindern.
de.70:42: So laß sie nur plaudern und sich vergnügen, bis sie ihrem Tag begegnen, der ihnen angedroht wird
de.70:43: dem Tag, an dem sie aus ihren Gräbern eilends hervorkommen, als eilten sie zu ihren Götzenfiguren.
de.70:44: Ihre Augen werden niedergeschlagen sein; Schmach wird sie bedecken. Das ist der Tag, der ihnen angedroht wird.

de.96:2: Er erschuf den Menschen aus einem Blutklumpen.
de.96:3: Lies; denn dein Herr ist Allgütig.
de.96:5: lehrt den Menschen, was er nicht wußte.
de.96:6: Keineswegs! Fürwahr, der Mensch übt Gewalttätigkeit
de.96:7: weil er sich im Reichtum sieht.
de.96:8: Fürwahr, zu deinem Herrn ist die Heimkehr.
de.96:9: Hast du den gesehen, der da verwehrt
de.96:11: Hast du gesehen, ob er auf dem rechten Weg ist
de.96:13: Hast du (den) gesehen, der ungläubig ist und sich abwendet?
de.96:14: Weiß er nicht, daß Allah (ihn) sieht?
de.96:15: Keineswegs! Wenn er nicht (davon) abläßt, werden Wir ihn gewiß ergreifen bei der Stirnlocke
de.96:17: er mag dann seine Mitverschworenen anrufen.
de.96:19: gehorche ihm doch nicht und wirf dich in Anbetung nieder und nahe dich (Allah).
de.97:1: Fürwahr, Wir haben ihn (den Quran) hinabgesandt in der Nacht von Al-Qadr.
de.97:2: Auch was lehrt dich wissen, ist? was die Nacht von Al-Qadr
de.97:3: Die Nacht von Al Qadr ist besser als tausend Monate.
de.97:4: In ihr steigen die Gottesboten und Gabriel herab mit der Erlaubnis ihres Herrn zu jeglichem Geheiß.
de.97:5: Frieden ist sie bis zum Anbruch der Morgenröte.
de.98:1: Diejenigen, die ungläubig sind unter dem Volk der Offenbarungsschrift und die Götzendiener können (von ihrem Irrtum) nichtbefreit werden, bis der deutliche Beweis zu ihnen kommt
de.98:2: ein Botschafter von Allah, der (ihnen) reinerhaltene (Quran-) Abschnitte verliest
de.98:4: Auch die, denen die Offenbarungsschrift gegeben wurde, waren nicht eher gespalten, alsbis der deutliche Beweis zu ihnen gekommen war.
de.98:5: Auch doch war ihnen nichts anderes befohlen worden, als Allah treu in lauterem Glauben zu dienen und das Gebet zu verrichten und die Zakah zu entrichten. Und das ist die Religion der Geradlinigkeit.
de.98:6: Fürwahr, jene, die ungläubig sind unter dem Volk der Offenbarungsschrift und die Götzendiener werden im Feuer der Gahannam sein; ewig werden sie darin bleiben; diese sind die schlechtesten der Geschöpfe.
de.98:7: Fürwahr, diejenigen aber, die glauben und gute Werke tun, sind die besten der Geschöpfe.
de.98:8: Ihr Lohn bei ihrem Herrn sind die Gärten von Eden, durcheilt von Bächen; ewig und immerdar werden sie darin verweilen. Allah ist mit ihnen wohlzufrieden und sie sind wohlzufrieden mit Ihm. Dies ist für den, der seinen Herrn fürchtet.
de.99:1: Wenn die Erde in aller Heftigkeit erbebt
de.99:2: und wenn die Erde ihre Lasten herausgibt
de.99:3: und wenn der Mensch sagt: "Was ist mit ihr?"
de.99:4: An jenem Tage wird sie ihre Geschichten erzählen
de.99:5: so wie ihr Herr (es) ihr eingegeben hat.
de.99:6: An jenem Tage kommen die Menschen in Gruppen zerstreut hervor, damit ihnen ihre Werke gezeigt werden.
de.99:7: Wer auch nur eines Stäubchens Gewicht Gutes tut, der wird es dann sehen.
de.99:8: Auch wer auch nur eines Stäubchens Gewicht Böses tut, der wird es dann sehen.

en.1:1: In the name of God, the Gracious, the Merciful.
en.1:2: Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.
en.1:3: The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
en.1:4: Master of the Day of Judgment.
en.1:5: It is You we worship, and upon You we call for help.
en.1:6: Guide us to the straight path.
en.1:7: The path of those You have blessed, not of those against whom there is anger, nor of those who are misguided.
en.10:1: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the Verses of the Wise Book.
en.10:2: Is it a wonder to the people that We inspired a man from among them: “Warn mankind, and give good news to those who believe that they are on a sound footing with their Lord”? The those who deny the truth said, “This is a manifest sorcerer.”
en.10:3: Your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then settled over the Throne, governing all things. There is no intercessor except after His permission. Such is God, your Lord—so serve Him. Will you not reflect?
en.10:4: To Him is your return, altogether. The promise of God is true. He originates creation, and then He repeats it, to reward those who believe and do good deeds with equity. As for those who disbelieve, for them is a drink of boiling water, and agonizing torment, on account of their disbelief.
en.10:5: It is He who made the sun radiant, and the moon a light, and determined phases for it—that you may know the number of years and the calculation. God did not create all this except with truth. He details the revelations for a people who know.
en.10:6: In the alternation of night and day, and in what God created in the heavens and the earth, are signs for people who are aware.
en.10:7: Those who do not hope to meet Us, and are content with the worldly life, and are at ease in it, and those who pay no heed to Our signs.
en.10:8: These—their dwelling is the Fire—on account of what they used to do.
en.10:9: As for those who believe and do good deeds, their Lord guides them in their faith. Rivers will flow beneath them in the Gardens of Bliss.
en.10:10: Their call therein is, “Glory be to You, our God.” And their greeting therein is, “Peace.” And the last of their call is, “Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.”
en.10:11: If God were to accelerate the ill for the people, as they wish to accelerate the good, their term would have been fulfilled. But We leave those who do not expect Our encounter to blunder in their excesses.
en.10:12: Whenever adversity touches the human being, he prays to Us—reclining on his side, or sitting, or standing. But when We have relieved his adversity from him, he goes away, as though he had never called on Us for trouble that had afflicted him. Thus the deeds of the transgressors appear good to them.
en.10:13: We destroyed generations before you when they did wrong. Their messengers came to them with clear signs, but they would not believe. Thus We requite the sinful people.
en.10:14: Then We made you successors on earth after them, to see how you would behave.
en.10:15: And when Our clear revelations are recited to them, those who do not hope to meet Us say, “Bring a Quran other than this, or change it.” Say, “It is not for me to change it of my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. I fear, if I disobeyed my Lord, the torment of a terrible Day.”
en.10:16: Say, “Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, and He would not have made it known to you. I have lived among you for a lifetime before it. Do you not understand?”
en.10:17: Who does greater wrong than someone who fabricates lies about God, or denies His revelations? The guilty will never prosper.
en.10:18: And they worship, besides God, what neither harms them nor benefits them. And they say, “These are our intercessors with God.” Say, “Are you informing God about what He does not know in the heavens or on earth?” Glorified be He, High above the associations they make.
en.10:19: Mankind was a single community; then they differed. Were it not for a prior decree from your Lord, the matters over which they had disputed would have been settled.
en.10:20: And they say, “If only a miracle was sent down to him from his Lord.” Say, “The realm of the unseen belongs to God; so wait, I am waiting with you.”
en.10:21: When We make the people taste mercy after some adversity has touched them, they begin to scheme against Our revelations. Say, “God is swifter in scheming.” Our envoys are writing down what you scheme.
en.10:22: It is He who transports you across land and sea. Until, when you are on ships, sailing in a favorable wind, and rejoicing in it, a raging wind arrives. The waves surge over them from every side, and they realize that they are besieged. Thereupon they pray to God, professing sincere devotion to Him: “If You save us from this, we will be among the appreciative.”
en.10:23: But then, when He has saved them, they commit violations on earth, and oppose justice. O people! Your violations are against your own souls. It is the enjoyment of the present life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.
en.10:24: The likeness of the present life is this: water that We send down from the sky is absorbed by the plants of the earth, from which the people and the animals eat. Until, when the earth puts on its fine appearance, and is beautified, and its inhabitants think that they have mastered it, Our command descends upon it by night or by day, and We turn it into stubble, as if it had not flourished the day before. We thus clarify the revelations for people who reflect.
en.10:25: God invites to the Home of Peace, and guides whomever He wills to a straight path.
en.10:26: For those who have done good is goodness, and more. Neither gloom nor shame will come over their faces. These are the inhabitants of the eternal Gardens, abiding therein forever.
en.10:27: As for those who have earned evil deeds: a reward of similar evil, and shame will cover them. They will have no defense against God—as if their faces are covered with dark patches of night. These are the inmates of the Fire, abiding therein forever.
en.10:28: On the Day when We will gather them altogether, then say to those who ascribed partners, “To your place, you and your partners.” Then We will separate between them, and their partners will say, “It was not us you were worshiping.”
en.10:29: “God is sufficient witness between us and you. We were unaware of your worshiping us.”
en.10:30: There, every soul will experience what it had done previously; and they will be returned to God, their True Master; and what they used to invent will fail them.
en.10:31: Say, “Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? And who controls the hearing and the sight? And who produces the living from the dead, and produces the dead from the living? And who governs the Order?” They will say, “God.” Say, “Will you not be careful?”
en.10:32: Such is God, your Lord—the True. What is there, beyond the truth, except falsehood? How are you turned away?
en.10:33: Thus your Lord’s Word proved true against those who disobeyed, for they do not believe.
en.10:34: Say, “Can any of your partners initiate creation, and then repeat it?” Say, “God initiates creation, and then repeats it. How are you so deluded?”
en.10:35: Say, “Can any of your partners guide to the truth?” Say, “God guides to the truth. Is He who guides to the truth more worthy of being followed, or he who does not guide, unless he himself is guided? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?”
en.10:36: Most of them follow nothing but assumptions; and assumptions avail nothing against the truth. God is fully aware of what they do.
en.10:37: This Quran could not have been produced by anyone other than God. In fact, it is a confirmation of what preceded it, and an elaboration of the Scripture. There is no doubt about it—it is from the Lord of the Universe.
en.10:38: Or do they say, “He has forged it”? Say, “Then produce a single chapter like it, and call upon whomever you can, apart from God, if you are truthful.”
en.10:39: In fact, they deny what is beyond the limits of their knowledge, and whose explanation has not yet reached them. Thus those before them refused to believe. So note the consequences for the evildoers.
en.10:40: Among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. Your Lord is fully aware of the mischief-makers.
en.10:41: If they accuse you of lying, say, “I have my deeds, and you have your deeds. You are quit of what I do, and I am quit of what you do.”
en.10:42: And among them are those who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?
en.10:43: And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind, even though they do not see?
en.10:44: God does not wrong the people in the least, but the people wrong their own selves.
en.10:45: On the Day when He rounds them up—as if they had tarried only one hour of a day—they will recognize one another. Those who denied the meeting with God will be the losers. They were not guided.
en.10:46: Whether We show you some of what We promise them, or take you, to Us is their return. God is witness to everything they do.
en.10:47: Every community has a messenger. When their messenger has come, judgment will be passed between them with fairness, and they will not be wronged.
en.10:48: And they say, “When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?”
en.10:49: Say, “I have no power to harm or benefit myself, except as God wills. To every nation is an appointed time. Then, when their time arrives, they can neither postpone it by one hour, nor advance it.
en.10:50: Say, “Have you considered? If His punishment overtakes you by night or by day, what part of it will the guilty seek to hasten?”
en.10:51: “Then, when it falls, will you believe in it? Now? When before you tried to hasten it?”
en.10:52: Then it will be said to those who did wrong, “Taste the torment of eternity. Will you be rewarded except for what you used to do?”
en.10:53: And they inquire of you, “Is it true?” Say, “Yes, by my Lord, it is true, and you cannot evade it.”
en.10:54: Had every soul which had done wrong possessed everything on earth, it would offer it as a ransom. They will hide the remorse when they witness the suffering, and it will be judged between them equitably, and they will not be wronged.
en.10:55: Assuredly, to God belongs everything in the heavens and the earth. Assuredly, the promise of God is true. But most of them do not know.
en.10:56: He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
en.10:57: O people! There has come to you advice from your Lord, and healing for what is in the hearts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.
en.10:58: Say, “In God’s grace and mercy let them rejoice. That is better than what they hoard.”
en.10:59: Say, “Have you considered the sustenance God has sent down for you, some of which you made unlawful, and some lawful?” Say, “Did God give you permission, or do you fabricate lies and attribute them to God?”
en.10:60: What will they think—those who fabricate lies and attribute them to God—on the Day of Resurrection? God is bountiful towards the people, but most of them do not give thanks.
en.10:61: You do not get into any situation, nor do you recite any Quran, nor do you do anything, but We are watching over you as you undertake it. Not even the weight of an atom, on earth or in the sky, escapes your Lord, nor is there anything smaller or larger, but is in a clear record.
en.10:62: Unquestionably, God’s friends have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve.
en.10:63: Those who believe and are aware.
en.10:64: For them is good news in this life, and in the Hereafter. There is no alteration to the words of God. That is the supreme triumph.
en.10:65: And let not their sayings dishearten you. All power is God’s. He is the Hearer, the Knower.
en.10:66: Certainly, to God belongs everyone in the heavens and everyone on earth. Those who invoke other than God do not follow partners; they follow only assumptions, and they only guess.
en.10:67: It is He who made the night for your rest, and the daylight for visibility. Surely in that are signs for people who listen.
en.10:68: And they said, “God has taken a son.” Be He glorified. He is the Self-Sufficient. His is everything in the heavens and everything on earth. Do you have any proof for this? Or are you saying about God what you do not know?
en.10:69: Say, “Those who fabricate lies about God will not succeed.”
en.10:70: Some enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment on account of their disbelief.
en.10:71: And relate to them the story of Noah, when he said to his people, “O my people, if my presence among you and my reminding you of God’s signs is too much for you, then in God I have put my trust. So come to a decision, you and your partners, and do not let the matter perplex you; then carry out your decision on me, and do not hold back.”
en.10:72: “But if you turn away, I have not asked you for any wage. My wage falls only on God, and I was commanded to be of those who submit.”
en.10:73: But they denounced him, so We saved him and those with him in the Ark, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who rejected Our signs. So consider the fate of those who were warned.
en.10:74: Then, after him, We sent messengers to their people. They came to them with the clear proofs, but they would not believe in anything they had already rejected. Thus We set a seal on the hearts of the hostile.
en.10:75: Then, after them, We sent Moses and Aaron with Our proofs to Pharaoh and his dignitaries. But they acted arrogantly. They were sinful people.
en.10:76: And when the truth came to them from Us, they said, “This is clearly sorcery.”
en.10:77: Moses said, “Is this what you say of the truth when it has come to you? Is this sorcery? Sorcerers do not succeed.”
en.10:78: They said, “Did you come to us to divert us from what we found our ancestors following, and so that you become prominent in the land? We will never believe in you.”
en.10:79: Pharaoh said, “Bring me every experienced sorcerer.”
en.10:80: And when the sorcerers came, Moses said to them, “Throw whatever you have to throw.”
en.10:81: And when they threw, Moses said, “What you produced is sorcery, and God will make it fail. God does not foster the efforts of the corrupt.”
en.10:82: “And God upholds the truth with His words, even though the sinners detest it.”
en.10:83: But none believed in Moses except some children of his people, for fear that Pharaoh and his chiefs would persecute them. Pharaoh was high and mighty in the land. He was a tyrant.
en.10:84: Moses said, “O my people, if you have believed in God, then put your trust in Him, if you have submitted.”
en.10:85: They said, “In God we have put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us victims of the oppressive people.”
en.10:86: “And deliver us, by Your mercy, from the disbelieving people.”
en.10:87: And We inspired Moses and his brother, “Settle your people in Egypt, and make your homes places of worship, and perform the devotional prayer (Ṣalāh), and give good news to the believers.”
en.10:88: Moses said, “Our Lord, you have given Pharaoh and his chiefs splendor and wealth in the worldly life. Our Lord, for them to lead away from Your path. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth, and harden their hearts, they will not believe until they see the painful torment.”
en.10:89: He said, “Your devotional prayer (Ṣalāh) has been answered, so go straight, and do not follow the path of those who do not know.”
en.10:90: And We delivered the Children of Israel across the sea. Pharaoh and his troops pursued them, defiantly and aggressively. Until, when he was about to drown, he said, “I believe that there is no god except the One the Children of Israel believe in, and I am of those who submit.”
en.10:91: Now? When you have rebelled before, and been of the mischief-makers?
en.10:92: Today We will preserve your body, so that you become a sign for those after you. But most people are heedless of Our signs.
en.10:93: And We settled the Children of Israel in a position of honor, and provided them with good things. They did not differ until knowledge came to them. Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding their differences.
en.10:94: If you are in doubt about what We revealed to you, ask those who read the Scripture before you. The truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be of those who doubt.
en.10:95: And do not be of those who deny God’s revelations, lest you become one of the losers.
en.10:96: Those against whom your Lord’s Word is justified will not believe.
en.10:97: Even if every sign comes to them—until they see the painful punishment.
en.10:98: If only there was one town that believed and benefited by its belief. Except for the people of Jonah. When they believed, We removed from them the suffering of disgrace in the worldly life, and We gave them comfort for a while.
en.10:99: Had your Lord willed, everyone on earth would have believed. Will you compel people to become believers?
en.10:100: No soul can believe except by God’s leave; and He lays disgrace upon those who refuse to understand.
en.10:101: Say, “Look at what is in the heavens and the earth.” But signs and warnings are of no avail for people who do not believe.
en.10:102: Do they expect anything but the likes of the days of those who passed away before them? Say, “Then wait, I will be waiting with you.”
en.10:103: Then We save Our messengers and those who believe. It is binding on Us to save the believers.
en.10:104: Say, “O people, if you are in doubt about my religion—I do not serve those you serve apart from God. But I serve God, the one who will terminate your lives. And I was commanded to be of the believers.”
en.10:105: And dedicate yourself to the true religion—a monotheist—and never be of the polytheists.
en.10:106: And do not call, apart from God, on what neither benefits you nor harms you. If you do, you are then one of the evildoers.
en.10:107: If God afflicts you with harm, none can remove it except He. And if He wants good for you, none can repel His grace. He makes it reach whomever He wills of His servants. He is the Forgiver, the Merciful.
en.10:108: Say, “O people, the truth has come to you from your Lord. Whoever accepts guidance is guided for his own soul; and whoever strays only strays to its detriment. I am not a guardian over you.”
en.10:109: And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until God issues His judgment, for He is the Best of judges.
en.100:6: Indeed, the human being is ungrateful to his Lord.
en.100:7: And he bears witness to that.
en.100:8: And he is fierce in his love of wealth.
en.100:9: Does he not know? When the contents of the graves are scattered around.
en.100:10: And the contents of the hearts are obtained.
en.100:11: Their Lord, on that Day, is fully informed of them.
en.101:3: What will explain to you what the Shocker is?
en.101:4: The Day when the people will be like scattered moths.
en.101:5: And the mountains will be like tufted wool.
en.101:6: As for he whose scales are heavy.
en.101:7: He will be in a pleasant life.
en.101:8: But as for he whose scales are light.
en.101:10: Do you know what it is?
en.102:5: If you knew with knowledge of certainty.
en.102:7: Then you will see it with the eye of certainty.
en.102:8: Then, on that Day, you will be questioned about the Bliss.
en.103:2: The human being is in loss.
en.103:3: Except those who believe, and do good works, and encourage truth, and recommend patience.
en.104:2: Who gathers wealth and counts it over.
en.104:3: Thinking that his wealth has made him immortal.
en.104:4: By no means. He will be thrown into the Crusher.
en.104:5: And what will make you realize what the Crusher is?
en.105:1: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the People of the Elephant?
en.105:2: Did He not make their plan go wrong?
en.105:3: He sent against them swarms of birds.
en.105:4: Throwing at them rocks of baked clay.
en.106:2: Their security during winter and summer journeys.
en.106:3: Let them worship the Lord of this House.
en.106:4: Who has fed them against hunger, and has secured them against fear.
en.107:1: Have you considered him who denies the religion?
en.107:2: It is he who mistreats the orphan.
en.107:3: And does not encourage the feeding of the poor.
en.107:4: So woe to those who pray.
en.107:5: Those who are heedless of their prayers.
en.107:6: Those who put on the appearance.
en.108:2: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.
en.108:3: He who hates you is the loser.
en.109:1: Say, “O those who deny the truth.
en.109:2: I do not worship what you worship.
en.109:3: Nor do you worship what I worship.
en.109:4: Nor do I serve what you serve.
en.109:5: Nor do you serve what I serve.
en.109:6: You have your way, and I have my way.”
en.11:1: Alif, Lam, Ra. A Scripture whose Verses were perfected, then elaborated, from One who is Wise and Informed.
en.11:2: That you shall worship none but God. “I am a warner to you from Him, and a bearer of good news.”
en.11:3: “And ask your Lord for forgiveness, and repent to Him. He will provide you with good sustenance until a stated term, and will bestow His grace on every possessor of virtue. But if you turn away, then I fear for you the punishment of a grievous Day.”
en.11:4: “To God is your return, and He is Capable of all things.”
en.11:5: They wrap their chests to hide from Him. But even as they cover themselves with their clothes, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. He knows what lies within the hearts.
en.11:6: There is no moving creature on earth but its sustenance depends on God. And He knows where it lives and where it rests. Everything is in a Clear Book.
en.11:7: It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days—and His Throne was upon the waters—in order to test you—which of you is best in conduct. And if you were to say, “You will be resurrected after death,” those who disbelieve would say, “This is nothing but plain witchcraft.”
en.11:8: And if We postponed their punishment until a stated time, they would say, “What holds it back?” On the Day when it reaches them, it will not be averted from them, and what they used to ridicule will besiege them.
en.11:9: If We give the human being a taste of mercy from Us, and then withdraw it from him, he becomes despairing and ungrateful.
en.11:10: And if We give him a taste of prosperity, after some adversity has afflicted him, he will say, “Troubles have gone away from me.” He becomes excited and proud.
en.11:11: Except those who are patient and do good deeds—these will have forgiveness and a great reward.
en.11:12: Perhaps you wish to disregard some of what is revealed to you, and you may be stressed because of it, since they say, “If only a treasure was sent down to him, or an angel came with him.” You are only a warner, and God is Responsible for all things.
en.11:13: Or do they say, “He invented it?” Say, “Then produce ten chapters like it, invented, and call upon whomever you can, besides God, if you are truthful.”
en.11:14: But if they fail to answer you, know that it was revealed with God’s knowledge, and that there is no god but He. Will you then submit?
en.11:15: Whoever desires the worldly life and its glitter—We will fully recompense them for their deeds therein, and therein they will not be defrauded.
en.11:16: These—they will have nothing but the Fire in the Hereafter. Their deeds are in vain therein, and their works are null.
en.11:17: Is he who possesses a clear proof from his Lord, recited by a witness from Him, and before it the Scripture of Moses, a guide and a mercy? These believe in it. But whoever defies it from among the various factions, the Fire is his promise. So have no doubt about it. It is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.
en.11:18: Who does greater wrong than he who fabricates lies about God? These will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, “These are they who lied about their Lord.” Indeed, the curse of God is upon the evildoers.
en.11:19: Those who hinder others from the path of God, and seek to make it crooked; and regarding the Hereafter, they are in denial.
en.11:20: These will not escape on earth, and they have no protectors besides God. The punishment will be doubled for them. They have failed to hear, and they have failed to see.
en.11:21: Those are the ones who lost their souls, and what they had invented has strayed away from them.
en.11:22: Without a doubt, in the Hereafter, they will be the biggest losers.
en.11:23: As for those who believe and do good deeds, and humble themselves before their Lord—these are the inhabitants of the eternal Gardens, where they will abide forever.
en.11:24: The parable of the two groups is that of the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Will you not reflect?
en.11:25: We sent Noah to his people, “I am to you a clear warner.”
en.11:26: “That you shall worship none but God. I fear for you the agony of a painful Day.”
en.11:27: The notables who disbelieved among his people said, “We see in you nothing but a man like us, and we see that only the worst among us have followed you, those of immature judgment. And we see that you have no advantage over us. In fact, we think you are liars.”
en.11:28: He said, “O my people, Have you considered? If I stand on clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me a mercy from Himself, but you were blind to it, can we compel you to accept it, even though you dislike it?”
en.11:29: “O my people! I ask of you no money for it. My reward lies only with God. And I am not about to dismiss those who believed; they will surely meet their Lord. And I see that you are ignorant people.”
en.11:30: “O my people! Who will support me against God, if I dismiss them? Will you not give a thought?”
en.11:31: “I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of God, nor do I know the future, nor do I say that I am an angel. Nor do I say of those who are despicable in your eyes that God will never give them any good. God is Aware of what lies in their souls. If I did, I would be one of the evildoers.”
en.11:32: They said, “O Noah, you have argued with us, and argued a great deal. Now bring upon us what you threaten us with, if you are truthful.”
en.11:33: He said, “It is God who will bring it upon you, if He wills, and you will not be able to escape.”
en.11:34: “My advice will not benefit you, much as I may want to advise you, if God desires to confound you. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.”
en.11:35: Or do they say, “He made it up?” Say, “If I made it up, upon me falls my crime, and I am innocent of the crimes you commit.”
en.11:36: And it was revealed to Noah: “None of your people will believe, except those who have already believed, so do not grieve over what they do.”
en.11:37: “And build the Ark, under Our eyes, and with Our inspiration, and do not address Me regarding those who did wrong; they are to be drowned.”
en.11:38: As he was building the ark, whenever some of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. He said, “If you ridicule us, we will ridicule you, just as you ridicule.”
en.11:39: “You will surely know upon whom will come a torment that will abase him, and upon whom will fall a lasting torment.”
en.11:40: Until, when Our command came, and the volcano erupted, We said, “Board into it a pair of every kind, and your family—except those against whom the sentence has already been passed—and those who have believed.” But those who believed with him were only a few.
en.11:41: He said, “Embark in it. In the name of God shall be its sailing and its anchorage. My Lord is indeed Forgiving and Merciful.”
en.11:42: And so it sailed with them amidst waves like hills. And Noah called to his son, who had kept away, “On my son! Embark with us, and do not be with the those who deny the truth.”
en.11:43: He said, “I will take refuge on a mountain—it will protect me from the water.” He said, “There is no protection from God’s decree today, except for him on whom He has mercy.” And the waves surged between them, and he was among the drowned.
en.11:44: And it was said, “O earth, swallow your waters,” and “O heaven, clear up.” And the waters receded, and the event was concluded, and it settled on Judi, and it was proclaimed: “Away with the wicked people.”
en.11:45: And Noah called to his Lord. He said, “O My Lord, my son is of my family, and Your promise is true, and You are the Wisest of the wise.”
en.11:46: He said, “O Noah, he is not of your family. It is an unrighteous deed. So do not ask Me about something you know nothing about. I admonish you, lest you be one of the ignorant.”
en.11:47: He said, “O My Lord, I seek refuge with You, from asking You about what I have no knowledge of. Unless You forgive me, and have mercy on me, I will be one of the losers.”
en.11:48: It was said, “O Noah, disembark with peace from Us; and with blessings upon you, and upon communities from those with you. And other communities We will grant prosperity, and then a painful torment from Us will befall them.”
en.11:49: These are some stories from the past that we reveal to you. Neither you, nor your people knew them before this. So be patient. The future belongs to the God-conscious.
en.11:50: And to Aad, their brother Hud. He said, “O my people, worship God, you have no other god besides Him. You do nothing but invent lies.”
en.11:51: “O my people, I ask you no wage for it; my wage lies with Him who originated me. Do you not understand?”
en.11:52: “O my people, ask forgiveness from your Lord, and repent to Him. He will release the sky pouring down upon you, and will add strength to your strength. And do not turn away and be wicked.”
en.11:53: They said, “O Hud, you did not bring us any evidence, and we are not about to abandon our gods at your word, and we are not believers in you.”
en.11:54: “We only say that some of our gods have possessed you with evil.” He said, “I call God to witness, and you to witness, that I am innocent of what you associate.
en.11:55: Besides Him. So scheme against me, all of you, and do not hesitate.
en.11:56: I have placed my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. There is not a creature but He holds it by the forelock. My Lord is on a straight path.
en.11:57: If you turn away, I have conveyed to you what I was sent to you with; and my Lord will replace you with another people, and you will not cause Him any harm. My Lord is Guardian over all things.”
en.11:58: And when Our decree came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us, and We delivered them from a harsh punishment.
en.11:59: That was Aad; they denied the signs of their Lord, and defied His messengers, and followed the lead of every stubborn tyrant.
en.11:60: And they were pursued by a curse in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Aad blasphemed against their Lord—so away with Aad, the people of Hud.
en.11:61: And to Thamood, their brother Saleh. He said, “O my people, worship God, you have no god other than Him. He initiated you from the earth, and settled you in it. So seek His forgiveness, and repent to Him. My Lord is Near and Responsive.”
en.11:62: They said, “O Saleh, we had hopes in you before this. Are you trying to prevent us from worshiping what our parents worship? We are in serious doubt regarding what you are calling us to.”
en.11:63: He said, “O my people, have you considered? If I stand upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Him, who would protect me from God, if I disobeyed Him? You add nothing for me except loss.”
en.11:64: “O my people, this is the she-camel of God, a sign for you. Let her graze on God’s land, and do not harm her, lest an imminent punishment overtakes you.”
en.11:65: But they hamstrung her, and so He said, “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. This is a prophecy that is infallible.”
en.11:66: Then, when Our command came, We saved Saleh and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us, from the disgrace of that day. Your Lord is the Strong, the Mighty.
en.11:67: And the Scream struck those who transgressed, and they became motionless bodies in their homes.
en.11:68: As if they had never prospered therein. Indeed, Thamood rejected their Lord, so away with Thamood.
en.11:69: Our messengers came to Abraham with good news. They said, “Peace.” He said, “Peace.” Soon after, he came with a roasted calf.
en.11:70: But when he saw their hands not reaching towards it, he became suspicious of them, and conceived a fear of them. They said, “Do not fear, we were sent to the people of Lot.”
en.11:71: His wife was standing by, so she laughed. And We gave her good news of Isaac; and after Isaac, Jacob.
en.11:72: She said, “Alas for me. Shall I give birth, when I am an old woman, and this, my husband, is an old man? This is truly a strange thing.”
en.11:73: They said, “Do you marvel at the decree of God? The mercy and blessings of God are upon you, O people of the house. He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.”
en.11:74: When Abraham's fear subsided, and the good news had reached him, he started pleading with Us concerning the people of Lot.
en.11:76: “O Abraham, refrain from this. The command of your Lord has come; they have incurred an irreversible punishment.”
en.11:77: And when Our envoys came to Lot, he was anxious for them, and concerned for them. He said, “This is a dreadful day.”
en.11:78: And his people came rushing towards him—they were in the habit of committing sins. He said, “O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear God, and do not embarrass me before my guests. Is there not one reasonable man among you?”
en.11:79: They said, “You know well that we have no right to your daughters, and you know well what we want.”
en.11:80: He said, “If only I had the strength to stop you, or could rely on some strong support.”
en.11:81: They said, “O Lot, we are the envoys of your Lord; they will not reach you. So set out with your family during the cover of the night, and let none of you look back, except for your wife. She will be struck by what will strike them. Their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?”
en.11:82: And when Our command came about, We turned it upside down, and We rained down on it stones of baked clay.
en.11:83: Marked from your Lord, and never far from the evildoers.
en.11:84: And to Median, their brother Shuaib. He said, “O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him. And do not short measure or short weight. I see you in good circumstances, but I fear for you the agony of an encompassing Day.”
en.11:85: “O my people! Give full measure and full weight, in all fairness, and do not cheat the people out of their rights, and do not spread corruption in the land.
en.11:86: What is left by God is best for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you.”
en.11:87: They said, “O Shuaib, does your devotional prayer (Ṣalāh) command you that we abandon what our ancestors worshiped, or doing with our wealth what we want? You are the one who is intelligent and wise.”
en.11:88: He said, “O my people, have you considered? What if I have clear evidence from my Lord, and He has given me good livelihood from Himself? I have no desire to do what I forbid you from doing. I desire nothing but reform, as far as I can. My success lies only with God. In Him I trust, and to Him I turn.”
en.11:89: “O my people, let not your hostility towards me cause you to suffer what was suffered by the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Saleh. The people of Lot are not far away from you.”
en.11:90: “And ask your Lord for forgiveness, and repent to Him. My Lord is Merciful and Loving.”
en.11:91: They said, “O Shuaib, we do not understand much of what you say, and we see that you are weak among us. Were it not for your tribe, we would have stoned you. You are of no value to us.”
en.11:92: He said, “O my people, is my tribe more important to you than God? And you have turned your backs on Him? My Lord comprehends everything you do.”
en.11:93: “O my people, do as you may, and so will I. You will know to whom will come a punishment that will shame him, and who is a liar. So look out; I am on the lookout with you.”
en.11:94: And when Our command came, We saved Shuaib and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and the Blast struck the evildoers, and they became motionless bodies in their homes.
en.11:95: As though they never flourished therein. Away with Median, as was done away with Thamood.
en.11:96: And We sent Moses with Our signs and a clear mandate.
en.11:97: To Pharaoh and his nobles, but they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not wise.
en.11:98: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection, and will lead them into the Fire. Miserable is the place he placed them in.
en.11:99: They were followed by a curse in this, and on the Day of Resurrection. Miserable is the path they followed.
en.11:100: These are of the reports of the towns—We relate them to you. Some are still standing, and some have withered away.
en.11:101: We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. Their gods, whom they invoked besides God, availed them nothing when the command of your Lord arrived. In fact, they added only to their ruin.
en.11:102: Such is the grip of your Lord when He seizes the towns in the midst of their sins. His grip is most painful, most severe.
en.11:103: In that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which humanity will be gathered together—that is a Day to be witnessed.
en.11:104: We only postpone it until a predetermined time.
en.11:105: On the Day when it arrives, no soul will speak without His permission. Some will be miserable, and some will be happy.
en.11:106: As for those who are miserable, they will be in the Fire. They will have therein sighing and wailing.
en.11:107: Remaining therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Your Lord is Doer of whatever He wills.
en.11:108: And as for those who are happy, they will be in the eternal Gardens, remaining therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills—a reward without end.
en.11:109: So be not in doubt regarding what these people worship. They worship only as their ancestors worshiped before. We will pay them their due in full, without any reduction.
en.11:110: We gave Moses the Scripture, but it was disputed. Were it not for a prior word from your Lord, it would have been settled between them. They are in serious doubt concerning it.
en.11:111: Your Lord will repay each one of them in full for their deeds. He is Aware of everything they do.
en.11:112: So be upright, as you are commanded, along with those who repented with you, and do not transgress. He is Seeing of everything you do.
en.11:113: And do not incline towards those who do wrong, or the Fire may touch you; and you will have no protectors besides God, and you will not be saved.
en.11:114: Perform the devotional prayer (Ṣalāh) at the borders of the day, and during the approaches of the night. The good deeds take away the bad deeds. This is a reminder for those who remember.
en.11:115: And be patient. God will not waste the reward of the virtuous.
en.11:116: If only there were, among the generations before you, people with wisdom, who spoke against corruption on earth—except for the few whom We saved. But the evildoers pursued the luxuries they were indulged in, and thus became guilty.
en.11:117: Your Lord would never destroy the towns wrongfully, while their inhabitants are righteous.
en.11:118: Had your Lord willed, He could have made humanity one community, but they continue to differ.
en.11:119: Except those on whom your Lord has mercy—for that reason He created them. The Word of your Lord is final: “I will fill the Inferno with jinn and humans, altogether.”
en.11:120: Everything We narrate to you of the history of the messengers is to strengthen your heart therewith. The truth has come to you in this, and a lesson, and a reminder for the believers.
en.11:121: And say to those who do not believe, “Act according to your ability; and so will we.”
en.11:123: To God belongs the future of the heavens and the earth, and to Him all authority goes back. So worship Him, and rely on Him. Your Lord is never unaware of what you do.
en.110:1: When there comes God’s victory, and conquest.
en.110:2: And you see the people entering God’s religion in multitudes.
en.110:3: Then celebrate the praise of your Lord, and seek His forgiveness. He is the Accepter of Repentance.
en.111:1: Condemned are the hands of Abee Lahab, and he is condemned.
en.111:2: His wealth did not avail him, nor did what he acquired.
en.111:3: He will burn in a Flaming Fire.
en.111:5: Around her neck is a rope of thorns.
en.112:3: He begets not, nor was He begotten.
en.112:4: And there is nothing comparable to Him.”
en.113:1: Say, “I take refuge with the Lord of Daybreak.
en.113:2: From the evil of what He created.
en.113:3: And from the evil of the darkness as it gathers.
en.113:4: And from the evil of those who practice sorcery.
en.113:5: And from the evil of an envious when he envies.”
en.114:1: Say, “I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.
en.114:4: From the evil of the sneaky whisperer.
en.114:5: Who whispers into the hearts of people.
en.114:6: From among jinn and among people.”
en.12:1: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the Verses of the Clear Book.
en.12:2: We have revealed it an Arabic Quran, so that you may understand.
en.12:3: We narrate to you the most accurate history, by revealing to you this Quran. Although, prior to it, you were of the unaware.
en.12:4: When Joseph said to his father, “O my father, I saw eleven planets, and the sun, and the moon; I saw them bowing down to me.”
en.12:5: He said, “O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot and scheme against you. the Adversary is man's sworn enemy.
en.12:6: And thus your Lord will choose you, and will teach you the interpretation of events, and will complete His blessing upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He has completed it before upon your forefathers Abraham and Isaac. Your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
en.12:7: In Joseph and his brothers are lessons for the seekers.
en.12:8: When they said, “Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, although we are a whole group. Our father is obviously in the wrong.
en.12:9: “Kill Joseph, or throw him somewhere in the land, and your father‘s attention will be yours. Afterwards, you will be decent people.”
en.12:10: One of them said, “Do not kill Joseph, but throw him into the bottom of the well; some caravan may pick him up—if you must do something.”
en.12:11: They said, “Father, why do you not trust us with Joseph, although we care for him?”
en.12:12: “Send him with us tomorrow, that he may roam and play; we will take care of him.”
en.12:13: He said, “It worries me that you would take him away. And I fear the wolf may eat him while you are careless of him.”
en.12:14: They said, “If the wolf ate him, and we are many, we would be good for nothing.”
en.12:15: So they went away with him, and agreed to put him at the bottom of the well. And We inspired him, “You will inform them of this deed of theirs when they are unaware.”
en.12:16: And they came to their father in the evening weeping.
en.12:17: They said, “O father, we went off racing one another, and left Joseph by our belongings; and the wolf ate him. But you will not believe us, even though we are being truthful.”
en.12:18: And they brought his shirt, with fake blood on it. He said, “Your souls enticed you to do something. But patience is beautiful, and God is my Help against what you describe.”
en.12:19: A caravan passed by, and they sent their water-carrier. He lowered his bucket, and said, “Good news. Here is a boy.” And they hid him as merchandise. But God was aware of what they did.
en.12:20: And they sold him for a cheap price—a few coins—they considered him to be of little value.
en.12:21: The Egyptian who bought him said to his wife, “Take good care of him; he may be useful to us, or we may adopt him as a son.” We thus established Joseph in the land, to teach him the interpretation of events. God has control over His affairs, but most people do not know.
en.12:22: When he reached his maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. We thus reward the virtuous.
en.12:23: She in whose house he was living tried to seduce him. She shut the doors, and said, “I am yours.” He said, “God forbid! He is my Lord. He has given me a good home. Sinners never succeed.”
en.12:24: She desired him, and he desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord. It was thus that We diverted evil and indecency away from him. He was one of Our loyal servants.
en.12:25: As they raced towards the door, she tore his shirt from behind. At the door, they ran into her husband. She said, “What is the penalty for him who desired to dishonor your wife, except imprisonment or a painful punishment?”
en.12:26: He said, “It was she who tried to seduce me.” A witness from her household suggested: “If his shirt is torn from the front: then she has told the truth, and he is the liar.
en.12:27: But if his shirt is torn from the back: then she has lied, and he is the truthful.”
en.12:28: And when he saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he said, “This is a woman's scheme. Your scheming is serious indeed.”
en.12:29: “Joseph, turn away from this. And you, woman, ask forgiveness for your sin; you are indeed in the wrong.”
en.12:30: Some ladies in the city said, “The governor's wife is trying to seduce her servant. She is deeply in love with him. We see she has gone astray.”
en.12:31: And when she heard of their gossip, she invited them, and prepared for them a banquet, and she gave each one of them a knife. She said, “Come out before them.” And when they saw him, they marveled at him, and cut their hands. They said, “Good God, this is not a human, this must be a precious angel.”
en.12:32: She said, “Here he is, the one you blamed me for. I did try to seduce him, but he resisted. But if he does not do what I tell him to do, he will be imprisoned, and will be one of the despised.”
en.12:33: He said, “My Lord, prison is more desirable to me than what they call me to. Unless You turn their scheming away from me, I may yield to them, and become one of the ignorant.”
en.12:34: Thereupon his Lord answered him, and diverted their scheming away from him. He is the Hearer, the Knower.
en.12:35: Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, to imprison him for a while.
en.12:36: Two youth entered the prison with him. One of them said, “I see myself pressing wine.” The other said, “I see myself carrying bread on my head, from which the birds are eating. Tell us their interpretation—we see that you are one of the virtuous.”
en.12:37: He said, “No food is served to you, but I have informed you about it before you have received it. That is some of what my Lord has taught me. I have forsaken the tradition of people who do not believe in God; and regarding the Hereafter, they are deniers.”
en.12:38: “And I have followed the faith of my forefathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with God. This is by virtue of God’s grace upon us and upon the people, but most people do not give thanks.
en.12:39: “O My fellow inmates, are diverse lords better, or God, the One, the Supreme?”
en.12:40: “You do not worship, besides Him, except names you have named, you and your ancestors, for which God has sent down no authority. Judgment belongs to none but God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. This is the right religion, but most people do not know.
en.12:41: “O my fellow inmates! One of you will serve his master wine; while the other will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. Thus the matter you are inquiring about is settled.”
en.12:42: And he said to the one he thought would be released, “Mention me to your master.” But the Adversary caused him to forget mentioning him to his master, so he remained in prison for several years.
en.12:43: The king said, “I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes, and others dried up. O elders, explain to me my vision, if you are able to interpret visions.”
en.12:44: They said, “Jumbles of dreams, and we know nothing of the interpretation of dreams.”
en.12:45: The one who was released said, having remembered after a time, “I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me out.”
en.12:46: “Joseph, O man of truth, inform us concerning seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green spikes, and others dried up, so that I may return to the people, so that they may know.”
en.12:47: He said, “You will farm for seven consecutive years. But whatever you harvest, leave it in its spikes, except for the little that you eat.”
en.12:48: Then after that will come seven difficult ones, which will consume what you have stored for them, except for the little that you have preserved.
en.12:49: Then after that will come a year that brings relief to the people, and during which they will press.
en.12:50: The king said, “Bring him to me.” And when the envoy came to him, he said, “Go back to your master, and ask him about the intentions of the women who cut their hands; my Lord is well aware of their schemes.”
en.12:51: He said, “What was the matter with you, women, when you tried to seduce Joseph?” They said, “God forbid! We knew of no evil committed by him.” The governor’s wife then said, “Now the truth is out. It was I who tried to seduce him, and he is telling the truth.”
en.12:52: “This is that he may know that I did not betray him in secret, and that God does not guide the scheming of the betrayers.”
en.12:53: “Yet I do not claim to be innocent. The soul commands evil, except those on whom my Lord has mercy. Truly my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.”
en.12:54: The king said, “Bring him to me, and I will reserve him for myself.” And when he spoke to him, he said, “This day you are with us established and secure.”
en.12:55: He said, “Put me in charge of the storehouses of the land; I am honest and knowledgeable.”
en.12:56: And thus We established Joseph in the land, to live therein wherever he wished. We touch with Our mercy whomever We will, and We never waste the reward of the virtuous.
en.12:57: But the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and observed piety.
en.12:58: And Joseph's brothers came, and entered into his presence. He recognized them, but they did not recognize him.
en.12:59: When he provided them with their provisions, he said, “Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I fill up the measure, and I am the best of hosts?”
en.12:60: “But if you do not bring him to me, you will have no measure from me, and you will not come near me.”
en.12:61: They said, “We will solicit him from his father. We will surely do.”
en.12:62: He said to his servants, “Put their goods in their saddlebags; perhaps they will recognize them when they return to their families, and maybe they will come back.”
en.12:63: When they returned to their father, they said, “O father, we were denied measure, but send our brother with us, and we will obtain measure. We will take care of him.”
en.12:64: He said, “Shall I trust you with him, as I trusted you with his brother before? God is the Best Guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
en.12:65: And when they opened their baggage, they found that their goods were returned to them. They said, “Father, what more do we want? Here are our goods, returned to us. We will provide for our family, and protect our brother, and have an additional camel-load. This is easy commerce.”
en.12:66: He said, “I will not send him with you, unless you give me a pledge before God that you will bring him back to me, unless you get trapped.” And when they gave him their pledge, he said, “God is witness to what we say.”
en.12:67: And he said, “O my sons, do not enter by one gate, but enter by different gates. I cannot avail you anything against God. The decision rests only with God. On Him I rely, and on Him let the reliant rely.”
en.12:68: And when they entered as their father had instructed them, it did not avail them anything against God; it was just a need in the soul of Jacob, which he carried out. He was a person of knowledge inasmuch as We had taught him, but most people do not know.
en.12:69: And when they entered into the presence of Joseph, he embraced his brother, and said, “I am your brother; do not be saddened by what they used to do.”
en.12:70: Then, when he provided them with their provisions, he placed the drinking-cup in his brother’s saddlebag. Then an announcer called out, “O people of the caravan, you are thieves.”
en.12:71: They said, as they came towards them, “What are you missing?”
en.12:72: They said, “We are missing the king’s goblet. Whoever brings it will have a camel-load; and I personally guarantee it.”
en.12:73: They said, “By God, you know we did not come to cause trouble in the land, and we are not thieves.”
en.12:74: They said, “What shall be his punishment, if you are lying?”
en.12:75: They said, “His punishment, if it is found in his bag: he will belong to you. Thus we penalize the guilty.”
en.12:76: So he began with their bags, before his brother's bag. Then he pulled it out of his brother’s bag. Thus We devised a plan for Joseph; he could not have detained his brother under the king’s law, unless God so willed. We elevate by degrees whomever We will; and above every person of knowledge, there is one more learned.
en.12:77: They said, “If he has stolen, a brother of his has stolen before.” But Joseph kept it to himself, and did not reveal it to them. He said, “You are in a worse situation, and God is Aware of what you allege.”
en.12:78: They said, “O noble prince, he has a father, a very old man, so take one of us in his place. We see that you are a good person.”
en.12:79: He said, “God forbid that we should arrest anyone except him in whose possession we found our property; for then we would be unjust.”
en.12:80: And when they despaired of him, they conferred privately. Their eldest said, “Don’t you know that your father received a pledge from you before God, and in the past you failed with regard to Joseph? I will not leave this land until my father permits me, or God decides for me; for He is the Best of Deciders.”
en.12:81: “Go back to your father, and say, ‘Our father, your son has stolen. We testify only to what we know, and we could not have prevented the unforeseen.’”
en.12:82: “Ask the town where we were, and the caravan in which we came. We are being truthful.”
en.12:83: He said, “Rather, your souls have contrived something for you. Patience is a virtue. Perhaps God will bring them all back to me. He is the Knowing, the Wise.”
en.12:84: Then he turned away from them, and said, “O my bitterness for Joseph.” And his eyes turned white from sorrow, and he became depressed.
en.12:85: They said, “By God, you will not stop remembering Joseph, until you have ruined your health, or you have passed away.”
en.12:86: He said, “I only complain of my grief and sorrow to God, and I know from God what you do not know.”
en.12:87: “O my sons, go and inquire about Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of God's comfort. None despairs of God's comfort except the disbelieving people.”
en.12:88: Then, when they entered into his presence, they said, “Mighty governor, adversity has befallen us, and our family. We have brought scant merchandise. But give us full measure, and be charitable towards us—God rewards the charitable.”
en.12:89: He said, “Do you realize what you did with Joseph and his brother, in your ignorance?”
en.12:90: They said, “Is that you, Joseph?” He said, “I am Joseph, and this is my brother. God has been gracious to us. He who practices piety and patience—God never fails to reward the virtuous.”
en.12:91: They said, “By God, God has preferred you over us. We were definitely in the wrong.”
en.12:92: He said, “There is no blame upon you today. God will forgive you. He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
en.12:93: “Take this shirt of mine, and lay it over my father’s face, and he will recover his sight. And bring your whole family to me.”
en.12:94: As the caravan set out, their father said, “I sense the presence of Joseph, though you may think I am senile.”
en.12:95: They said, “By God, you are still in your old confusion.”
en.12:96: Then, when the bearer of good news arrived, he laid it over his face, and he regained his sight. He said, “Did I not say to you that I know from God what you do not know?”
en.12:97: They said, “Father, pray for the forgiveness of our sins; we were indeed at fault.”
en.12:98: He said, “I will ask my Lord to forgive you. He is the Forgiver, the Most Merciful.”
en.12:99: Then, when they entered into the presence of Joseph, he embraced his parents, and said, “Enter Egypt, God willing, safe and secure.”
en.12:100: And he elevated his parents on the throne, and they fell prostrate before him. He said, “Father, this is the fulfillment of my vision of long ago. My Lord has made it come true. He has blessed me, when he released me from prison, and brought you out of the wilderness, after the devil had sown conflict between me and my brothers. My Lord is Most Kind towards whomever He wills. He is the All-knowing, the Most Wise.”
en.12:101: “My Lord, You have given me some authority, and taught me some interpretation of events. Initiator of the heavens and the earth; You are my Protector in this life and in the Hereafter. Receive my soul in submission, and unite me with the virtuous.”
en.12:102: This is news from the past that We reveal to you. You were not present with them when they plotted and agreed on a plan.
en.12:103: But most people, for all your eagerness, are not believers.
en.12:104: You ask them no wage for it. It is only a reminder for all mankind.
en.12:105: How many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, paying no attention to them?
en.12:106: And most of them do not believe in God unless they associate others.
en.12:107: Do they feel secure that a covering of God’s punishment will not come upon them, or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware?
en.12:108: Say, “This is my way; I invite to God, based on clear knowledge—I and whoever follows me. Glory be to God; and I am not of the polytheists.”
