en.12:109: We did not send before you except men, whom We inspired, from the people of the towns. Have they not roamed the earth and seen the consequences for those before them? The Home of the Hereafter is better for those who are righteous. Do you not understand?
en.12:110: Until, when the messengers have despaired, and thought that they were rejected, Our help came to them. We save whomever We will, and Our severity is not averted from the guilty people.
en.12:111: In their stories is a lesson for those who possess intelligence. This is not a fabricated tale, but a confirmation of what came before it, and a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance, and mercy for people who believe.
en.13:1: Alif, Lam, Meem, Ra. These are the signs of the Scripture. What is revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.
en.13:2: God is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, and then settled on the Throne. And He regulated the sun and the moon, each running for a specified period. He manages all affairs, and He explains the signs, that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord.
en.13:3: And it is He who spread the earth, and placed in it mountains and rivers. And He placed in it two kinds of every fruit. He causes the night to overlap the day. In that are signs for people who reflect.
en.13:4: On earth are adjacent terrains, and gardens of vines, and crops, and date-palms, from the same root or from distinct roots, irrigated with the same water. We make some taste better than others. In that are proofs for people who reason.
en.13:5: Should you wonder—the real wonder is their saying: “When we have become dust, will we be in a new creation?” Those are they who defied their Lord. Those are they who will have yokes around their necks. Those are the inhabitants of the Fire, where they will remain forever.
en.13:6: And they urge you to hasten evil before good, though examples have passed away before them. Your Lord is full of forgiveness towards the people for their wrongdoings, yet your Lord is severe in retribution.
en.13:7: Those who disbelieve say, “Why was a miracle not sent down to him from his Lord?” You are only a warner, and to every community is a guide.
en.13:8: God knows what every female bears, and every increase and decrease of the wombs. With Him, everything is by measure.
en.13:9: The Knower of the Invisible and the Visible; the Grand, the Supreme.
en.13:10: It is the same; whether one of you conceals his speech, or declares it; whether he goes into hiding by night, or goes out by day.
en.13:11: He has a succession; before him and behind him, protecting him by God’s command. God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves. And if God wills any hardship for a people, there is no turning it back;, and apart from Him they have no protector.
en.13:12: It is He who shows you the lightening, causing fear and hope. And He produces the heavy clouds.
en.13:13: The thunder praises His glory, and so do the divine messengers, in awe of Him. And He sends the thunderbolts, striking with them whomever He wills. Yet they argue about God, while He is Tremendous in might.
en.13:14: To Him belongs the call to truth. Those they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with anything—except as someone who stretches his hands towards water, so that it may reach his mouth, but it does not reach it. The prayers of the unbelievers are only in vain.
en.13:15: To God prostrates everyone in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows, in the morning and in the evening.
en.13:16: Say, “Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?” Say, “God.” Say, “Have you taken besides Him protectors, who have no power to profit or harm even themselves?” Say, “Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are darkness and light equal? Or have they assigned to God associates, who created the likes of His creation, so that the creations seemed to them alike? Say, “God is the Creator of all things, and He is The One, the Irresistible.”
en.13:17: He sends down water from the sky, and riverbeds flow according to their capacity. The current carries swelling froth. And from what they heat in fire of ornaments or utensils comes a similar froth. Thus God exemplifies truth and falsehood. As for the froth, it is swept away, but what benefits the people remains in the ground. Thus God presents the analogies.
en.13:18: For those who respond to their Lord is the best. But as for those who do not respond to Him, even if they possessed everything on earth, and twice as much, they could not redeem themselves with it. Those will have the worst reckoning; and their home is the Inferno—a miserable destination.
en.13:19: Is he who knows that what was revealed to your from your Lord is the truth, like him who is blind? Only those who reason will remember.
en.13:20: Those who fulfill the promise to God, and do not violate the agreement.
en.13:21: And those who join what God has commanded to be joined, and fear their Lord, and dread the dire reckoning.
en.13:22: And those who patiently seek the presence of their Lord, and pray regularly, and spend from Our provisions to them, secretly and openly, and repel evil with good. These will have the Ultimate Home.
en.13:23: Everlasting Gardens, which they will enter, along with the virtuous among their parents, and their spouses, and their descendants. And the divine messengers will enter upon them from every gate.
en.13:24: “Peace be upon you, because you endured patiently. How excellent is the Final Home.”
en.13:25: As for those who violate the promise to God, after pledging to keep it, and sever what God has commanded to be joined, and spread corruption on earth—these, the curse will be upon them, and they will have the Worst Home.
en.13:26: God dispenses the provisions to whomever He wills, and restricts. And they delight in the worldly life; yet the worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is only enjoyment.
en.13:27: Those who disbelieve say, “If only a miracle was sent down to him from his Lord.” Say, “God leads astray whomever He wills, and He guides to Himself whoever repents.”
en.13:28: Those who believe, and whose hearts find comfort in the remembrance of God. Surely, it is in the remembrance of God that hearts find comfort.”
en.13:29: For those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them is happiness and a beautiful return.
en.13:30: Thus We sent you among a community before which other communities have passed away, that you may recite to them what We revealed to you. Yet they deny the Benevolent One. Say, “He is my Lord; there is no god but He; in Him I trust, and to Him is my repentance.”
en.13:31: Even if there were a Quran, by which mountains could be set in motion, or by which the earth could be shattered, or by which the dead could be made to speak. In fact, every decision rests with God. Did the believers not give up and realize that had God willed, He would have guided all humanity? Disasters will continue to strike those who disbelieve, because of their deeds, or they fall near their homes, until God’s promise comes true. God never breaks a promise.
en.13:32: Messengers before you were ridiculed, but I granted the those who deny the truth respite, and then I seized them. What a punishment it was!
en.13:33: Is He who is watchful over the deeds of every soul? Yet they ascribe associates to God. Say, “Name them! Or are you informing Him of something on earth He does not know, or is it a show of words?” In fact, the scheming of those who disbelieve is made to appear good to them, and they are averted from the path. Whomever God misguides has no guide.
en.13:34: There is for them torment in the worldly life, but the torment of the Hereafter is harsher. And they have no defender against God.
en.13:35: The likeness of the Garden of Paradise promised to the virtuous: rivers flowing beneath it; its food is perpetual, and so is its shade. Such is the sequel for those who guard against evil, but the sequel of the those who deny the truth is the Fire.
en.13:36: Those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what was revealed to you, while some factions reject parts of it. Say, “I am commanded to worship God, and to never associate anything with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return.”
en.13:37: Thus We revealed it an Arabic code of law. Were you to follow their desires, after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have neither ally nor defender against God.
en.13:38: We sent messengers before you, and We assigned for them wives and offspring. No messenger could bring a sign except with the permission of God. For every era is a scripture.
en.13:39: God abolishes whatever He wills, and He affirms. With Him is the source of the Scripture.
en.13:40: Whether We show you some of what We have promised them, or We cause you to die—your duty is to inform, and Ours is the reckoning.
en.13:41: Do they not see how We deal with the earth, diminishing it at its edges? God judges; and nothing can hold back His judgment. And He is quick to settle accounts.
en.13:42: Those before them planned, but the entire plan is up to God. He knows what every soul earns. Those who disbelieve will know to whom the Ultimate Home is.
en.13:43: Those who disbelieve say, “You are not a messenger.” Say, “God is a sufficient witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture.”
en.14:1: Alif, Lam, Ra. A Scripture that We revealed to you, that you may bring humanity from darkness to light—with the permission of their Lord—to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.
en.14:2: God—to whom belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. And woe to the those who deny the truth from a severe torment.
en.14:3: Those who prefer the present life to the Hereafter, and repel from the path of God, and seek to make it crooked—these are far astray.
en.14:4: We never sent any messenger except in the language of his people, to make things clear for them. God leads astray whom He wills, and guides whom He wills. He is the Mighty, the Wise.
en.14:5: We sent Moses with Our signs: “Bring your people out of darkness into light, and remind them of the Days of God.” In that are signs for every patient and thankful person.”
en.14:6: Moses said to his people, “Remember God’s blessings upon you, as He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who inflicted on you terrible suffering, slaughtering your sons while sparing your daughters. In that was a serious trial from your Lord.”
en.14:7: And when your Lord proclaimed: “If you give thanks, I will grant you increase; but if you are ungrateful, My punishment is severe.”
en.14:8: And Moses said, “Even if you are ungrateful, together with everyone on earth—God is in no need, Worthy of Praise.”
en.14:9: Has not the story reached you, of those before you, the people of Noah, and Aad, and Thamood—and those after them? None knows them except God. Their messengers came to them with the clear proofs, but they tried to silence them, and said, “We reject what you are sent with, and we are in serious doubt regarding what you are calling us to.”
en.14:10: Their messengers said, “Is there any doubt about God, Maker of the heavens and the earth? He calls you to forgive you your sins, and to defer you until a stated term.” They said, “You are only humans like us; you want to turn us away from what our ancestors worshiped; so bring us a clear proof.”
en.14:11: Their messengers said to them, “We are only humans like you, but God favors whomever He wills from among His servants. We cannot possibly show you any proof, except by leave of God. In God let the faithful put their trust.”
en.14:12: “And why should we not trust in God, when He has guided us in our ways? We will persevere in the face of your persecution. And upon God the reliant should rely.”
en.14:13: Those who disbelieved said to their messengers, “We will expel you from our land, unless you return to our religion.” And their Lord inspired them: “We will destroy the evildoers.”
en.14:14: “And We will settle you in the land after them. That is for him who fears My Majesty, and fears My threats.”
en.14:15: And they prayed for victory, and every stubborn tyrant came to disappointment.
en.14:16: Beyond him lies the Inferno, and he will be given to drink putrid water.
en.14:17: He will guzzle it, but he will not swallow it. Death will come at him from every direction, but he will not die. And beyond this is relentless suffering.
en.14:18: The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their works are like ashes, in a fierce wind, on a stormy day. They have no control over anything they have earned. That is the utmost misguidance.
en.14:19: Do you not see that God created the heavens and the earth with truth? If He wills, He can do away with you, and bring a new creation.
en.14:20: And that is not difficult for God.
en.14:21: They will emerge before God, altogether. The weak will say to those who were proud, “We were your followers, can you protect us at all against God’s punishment?” They will say, “Had God guided us, we would have guided you. It is the same for us; whether we mourn, or are patient; there is no asylum for us.”
en.14:22: And the Adversary will say, when the issue is settled, “God has promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you, except that I called you, and you answered me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot come to your aid, nor can you come to my aid. I reject your associating with me in the past. The evildoers will have a torment most painful.”
en.14:23: But those who believed and did good deeds will be admitted into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to remain therein forever, by leave of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be: “Peace.”
en.14:24: Do you not see how God presents a parable? A good word is like a good tree—its root is firm, and its branches are in the sky.
en.14:25: It yields its fruits every season by the will of its Lord. God presents the parables to the people, so that they may reflect.
en.14:26: And the parable of a bad word is that of a bad tree—it is uprooted from the ground; it has no stability.
en.14:27: God gives firmness to those who believe, with the firm word, in this life, and in the Hereafter. And God leads the wicked astray. God does whatever He wills.
en.14:28: Have you not seen those who exchanged the blessing of God with blasphemy, and landed their people into the house of perdition?
en.14:29: the Inferno—they will roast in it. What a miserable settlement.
en.14:30: And they set up rivals to God, in order to lead away from His path. Say, “Enjoy yourselves; your destination is the Fire.”
en.14:31: Tell My servants who have believed to perform the prayers, and to give from what We have given them, secretly and publicly, before a Day comes in which there is neither trading nor friendship.
en.14:32: God is He Who created the heavens and the earth, and sends down water from the sky, and with it produces fruits for your sustenance. And He committed the ships to your service, sailing through the sea by His command, and He committed the rivers to your service.
en.14:33: And He committed the sun and the moon to your service, both continuously pursuing their courses, and He committed the night and the day to your service.
en.14:34: And He has given you something of all what you asked. And if you were to count God’s blessings, you would not be able to enumerate them. The human being is unfair and ungrateful.
en.14:35: Recall that Abraham said, “O my Lord, make this land peaceful, and keep me and my sons from worshiping idols.”
en.14:36: “My Lord, they have led many people astray. Whoever follows me belongs with me; and whoever disobeys me—You are Forgiving and Merciful.
en.14:37: “Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley of no vegetation, by Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may perform the prayers. So make the hearts of some people incline towards them, and provide them with fruits, that they may be thankful.”
en.14:38: “Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we reveal. And nothing is hidden from God, on earth or in the heaven.”
en.14:39: “Praise be to God, Who has given me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac. My Lord is the Hearer of Prayers.”
en.14:40: “My Lord, make me one who performs the devotional prayer (Ṣalāh), and from my offspring. Our Lord, accept my supplication.”
en.14:41: “Our Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and the believers, on the Day the Reckoning takes place.”
en.14:42: Do not ever think that God is unaware of what the evildoers do. He only defers them until a Day when the sights stare.
en.14:43: Their necks outstretched, their heads upraised, their gaze unblinking, their hearts void.
en.14:44: And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come upon them, and the wicked will say, “Our Lord, defer us for a little while, and we will answer Your call and follow the messengers.” Did you not swear before that there will be no passing away for you?
en.14:45: And you inhabited the homes of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We cited for you the examples.
en.14:46: They planned their plans, but their plans are known to God, even if their plans can eliminate mountains.
en.14:47: Do not ever think that God will break His promise to His messengers. God is Strong, Able to Avenge.
en.14:48: On the Day when the earth is changed into another earth, and the heavens, and they will emerge before God, the One, the Irresistible.
en.14:49: On that Day, you will see the sinners bound together in chains.
en.14:50: Their garments made of tar, and the Fire covering their faces.
en.14:51: That God may repay each soul according to what it has earned. God is Quick in reckoning.
en.14:52: This is a proclamation for mankind, that they may be warned thereby, and know that He is One God, and that people of understanding may remember.
en.15:1: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the Verses of the Scripture; a Quran that makes things clear.
en.15:2: Perhaps those who disbelieve would like to become Muslims.
en.15:3: Leave them to eat, and enjoy, and be lulled by hope. They will find out.
en.15:4: We have never destroyed a town unless it had a set time.
en.15:5: No nation can bring its time forward, nor can they delay it.
en.15:6: And they said, “O you who received the message, you are insane.”
en.15:7: Why do you not bring us the divine messengers, if you are truthful?”
en.15:8: We do not send the divine messengers down except with reason, and they will not be held back.
en.15:9: Surely We revealed the Message, and We will surely preserve it.
en.15:10: We sent others before you, to the former communities.
en.15:11: But no messenger came to them, but they ridiculed him.
en.15:12: Thus We slip it into the hearts of the guilty.
en.15:13: They do not believe in it, though the ways of the ancients have passed away.
en.15:14: Even if We opened for them a gateway into the sky, and they began to ascend through it.
en.15:15: They would still say, “Our eyes are hallucinating; in fact, we are people bewitched.”
en.15:16: We placed constellations in the sky, and made them beautiful to the beholders.
en.15:17: And We guarded them from every outcast devil.
en.15:18: Except one who steals a hearing, and is followed by a visible projectile.
en.15:19: We spread the earth, and placed stabilizers in it, and in it We grew all things in proper measure.
en.15:20: And in it We created livelihoods for you, and for those for whom you are not the providers.
en.15:21: There is not a thing but with Us are its stores, and We send it down only in precise measure.
en.15:22: We send the fertilizing winds; and send down water from the sky, and give it to you to drink, and you are not the ones who store it.
en.15:23: It is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors.
en.15:24: And We know those of you who go forward, and We know those who lag behind.
en.15:25: It is your Lord who will gather them together. He is the Wise, the Knowing.
en.15:26: We created the human being from clay, from molded mud.
en.15:27: And the jinn We created before, from piercing fire.
en.15:28: Your Lord said to the divine messengers, “I am creating a human being from clay, from molded mud.”
en.15:29: “When I have formed him, and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down prostrating before him.”
en.15:30: So the divine messengers prostrated themselves, all together.
en.15:31: Except for the Adversary. He refused to be among those who prostrated themselves.
en.15:32: He said, “O the Adversary, what kept you from being among those who prostrated themselves?”
en.15:33: He said, “I am not about to prostrate myself before a human being, whom You created from clay, from molded mud.”
en.15:34: He said, “Then get out of here, for you are an outcast”.
en.15:35: “And the curse will be upon you until the Day of Judgment.”
en.15:36: He said, “My Lord, reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.”
en.15:37: He said, “You are of those reprieved.”
en.15:38: “Until the Day of the time appointed.”
en.15:39: He said, “My Lord, since You have lured me away, I will glamorize for them on earth, and I will lure them all away.”
en.15:40: “Except for Your sincere servants among them.”
en.15:41: He said, “This is a right way with Me.”
en.15:42: “Over My servants you have no authority, except for the sinners who follow you.”
en.15:43: And the Inferno is the meeting-place for them all.
en.15:44: “It has seven doors; for each door is an assigned class.”
en.15:45: But the virtuous will be in gardens with springs.
en.15:47: And We will remove all ill-feelings from their hearts—brothers and sisters, on couches facing one another.
en.15:48: No fatigue will ever touch them therein, nor will they be asked to leave it.
en.15:49: Inform My servants that I am the Forgiver, the Merciful.
en.15:50: And that My punishment is the painful punishment.
en.15:51: And inform them of the guests of Abraham.
en.15:52: When they entered upon him, and said, “Peace.” He said, “We are wary of you.”
en.15:53: They said, “Do not fear; we bring you good news of a boy endowed with knowledge.”
en.15:54: He said, “Do you bring me good news, when old age has overtaken me? What good news do you bring?”
en.15:55: They said, “We bring you good news in truth, so do not despair.”
en.15:56: He said, “And who despairs of his Lord’s mercy but the lost?”
en.15:57: He said, “So what is your business, O envoys?”
en.15:58: They said, “We were sent to a sinful people.”
en.15:59: “Except for the family of Lot; we will save them all.”
en.15:60: “Except for his wife.” We have determined that she will be of those who lag behind.
en.15:61: And when the envoys came to the family of Lot.
en.15:62: He said, “You are a people unknown to me.”
en.15:63: They said, “We bring you what they have doubts about.”
en.15:64: “We bring you the truth, and we are truthful.”
en.15:65: “Travel with your family at the dead of the night, and follow up behind them, and let none of you look back, and proceed as commanded.”
en.15:66: And We informed him of Our decree: the last remnant of these will be uprooted by early morning.
en.15:67: And the people of the town came joyfully.
en.15:68: He said, “These are my guests, so do not embarrass me.”
en.15:69: “And fear God, and do not disgrace me.”
en.15:70: They said, “Did we not forbid you from strangers?”
en.15:71: He said, “These are my daughters, if you must.”
en.15:72: By your life, they were blundering in their drunkenness.
en.15:73: So the Blast struck them at sunrise.
en.15:74: And We turned it upside down, and rained down upon them stones of baked clay.
en.15:75: Surely in that are lessons for those who read signs.
en.15:76: And it is on an existing road.
en.15:77: Surely in that is a sign for the believers.
en.15:78: The people of the Woods were also evildoers.
en.15:79: So We took revenge upon them. Both are clearly documented.
en.15:80: The people of the Rock also rejected the messengers.
en.15:81: We gave them Our revelations, but they turned away from them.
en.15:82: They used to carve homes in the mountains, feeling secure.
en.15:83: But the Blast struck them in the morning.
en.15:84: All they had acquired was of no avail to them.
en.15:85: We did not create the heavens and the earth, and what lies between them, except with truth. The Hour is coming, so forgive with gracious forgiveness.
en.15:86: Your Lord is the All-Knowing Creator.
en.15:87: We have given you seven of the pairs, and the Grand Quran.
en.15:88: Do not extend your eyes towards what We have bestowed on some couples of them to enjoy, and do not grieve over them, and lower your wing to the believers.
en.15:89: And say, “I am the clear warner.”
en.15:90: Just as We sent down to the separatists.
en.15:91: Those who made the Quran obsolete.
en.15:92: By your Lord, we will question them all.
en.15:93: About what they used to do.
en.15:94: So proclaim openly what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists.
en.15:95: We are enough for you against the mockers.
en.15:96: Those who set up another god with God. They will come to know.
en.15:97: We are aware that your heart is strained by what they say.
en.15:98: So glorify the praise of your Lord, and be among those who bow down.
en.15:99: And worship your Lord in order to attain certainty.
en.16:1: The command of God has come, so do not rush it. Glory be to Him; exalted above what they associate.
en.16:2: He sends down the divine messengers with the Spirit by His command, upon whom He wills of His servants: “Give warning that there is no god but Me, and fear Me.”
en.16:3: He created the heavens and the earth with justice. He is exalted above the associations they attribute.
en.16:4: He created the human being from a drop of fluid, yet he becomes an open adversary.
en.16:5: And the livestock—He created them for you. In them are warmth and benefits for you, and of them you eat.
en.16:6: And there is beauty in them for you, when you bring them home, and when you drive them to pasture.
en.16:7: And they carry your loads to territory you could not have reached without great hardship. Your Lord is Clement and Merciful.
en.16:8: And the horses, and the mules, and the donkeys—for you to ride, and for luxury. And He creates what you do not know.
en.16:9: It is for God to point out the paths, but some of them are flawed. Had He willed, He could have guided you all.
en.16:10: It is He Who sends down for you from the sky water. From it is drink, and with it grows vegetation for grazing.
en.16:11: And He produces for you grains with it, and olives, and date-palms, and grapes, and all kinds of fruits. Surely in that is a sign for people who think.
en.16:12: And He regulated for you the night and the day; and the sun, and the moon, and the stars are disposed by His command. Surely in that are signs for people who ponder.
en.16:13: And whatsoever He created for you on earth is of diverse colors. Surely in that is a sign for people who are mindful.
en.16:14: And it is He who made the sea to serve you, that you may eat from it tender meat, and extract from it ornaments that you wear. And you see the ships plowing through it, as you seek His bounties, so that you may give thanks.
en.16:15: And he cast mountains on the earth, lest it shifts with you; and rivers, and roads, so that you may be guided.
en.16:16: And landmarks. And by the stars they guide themselves.
en.16:17: Is He who creates like him who does not create? Will you not take a lesson?
en.16:18: And if you tried to enumerate the favors of God, you will not be able to count them. God is Forgiving and Merciful.
en.16:19: And God knows what you hide and what you disclose.
en.16:20: Those they invoke besides God create nothing, but are themselves created.
en.16:21: They are dead, not alive; and they do not know when they will be resurrected.
en.16:22: Your God is one God. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial, and they are arrogant.
en.16:23: Without a doubt, God knows what they conceal and what they reveal. He does not like the arrogant.
en.16:24: And when it is said to them, “What has your Lord sent down?” They say, “Legends of the ancients.”
en.16:25: So let them carry their loads complete on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the loads of those they misguided without knowledge. Evil is what they carry.
en.16:26: Those before them also schemed, but God took their structures from the foundations, and the roof caved in on them. The punishment came at them from where they did not perceive.
en.16:27: Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will disgrace them, and say, “Where are My associates for whose sake you used to dispute?” Those who were given knowledge will say, “Today shame and misery are upon the those who deny the truth.”
en.16:28: Those wronging their souls while the divine messengers are taking them away—they will propose peace: “We did no wrong.” Yes you did. God is aware of what you used to do.”
en.16:29: Enter the gates of the Inferno, to dwell therein forever. Miserable is the residence of the arrogant.
en.16:30: And it will be said to those who maintained piety, “What has your Lord revealed?” They will say, “Goodness.” To those who do good in this world is goodness, and the Home of the Hereafter is even better. How wonderful is the residence of the God-conscious.
en.16:31: The Gardens of Perpetuity, which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow, where they will have whatever they desire. Thus God rewards the God-conscious.
en.16:32: Those who are in a wholesome state when the divine messengers take them—will say, “Peace be upon you; enter the eternal Gardens, for what you used to do.”
en.16:33: Are they but waiting for the divine messengers to come to them, or for the command of your Lord to arrive? Those before them did likewise. God did not wrong them, but they used to wrong their own souls.
en.16:34: So the evils of their deeds assailed them, and what they used to ridicule engulfed them.
en.16:35: The idolaters say, “Had God willed, we would not have worshiped anything besides Him, neither us, nor our ancestors, nor would we have prohibited anything besides His prohibitions.” Those before them did likewise. Are the messengers responsible for anything but clear communication?
en.16:36: To every community We sent a messenger: “Worship God, and avoid idolatry.” Some of them God guided, while others deserved misguidance. So travel through the earth, and see what the fate of the deniers was.
en.16:37: Even though you may be concerned about their guidance, God does not guide those who misguide. And they will have no saviors.
en.16:38: And they swear by God with their most solemn oaths, “God will not resurrect anyone who dies.” Yes indeed, it is a promise binding on Him, but most people do not know.
en.16:39: To clarify for them what they differed about, and for the faithless to know that they were liars.
en.16:40: When We intend for something to happen, We say to it, “Be,” and it becomes.
en.16:41: Those who emigrate for God’s sake after being persecuted, We will settle them in a good place in this world; but the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
en.16:42: Those who endure patiently, and in their Lord they put their trust.
en.16:43: We did not send before you except men whom We inspired. So ask the people of knowledge, if you do not know.
en.16:44: With the clarifications and the scriptures. And We revealed to you the Reminder, that you may clarify to the people what was revealed to them, and that they may reflect.
en.16:45: Do those who scheme evils feel secure that God will not cause the earth to cave in with them, or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?
en.16:46: Or that He will not seize them during their activities? And they will not be able to prevent it.
en.16:47: Or that He will not seize them while in dread? Your Lord is Gentle and Merciful.
en.16:48: Have they not observed what God has created? Their shadows revolve from the right and the left, bowing to God as they shrink away.
en.16:49: To God bows down everything in the heavens and everything on earth—every living creature, and the divine messengers, and without being proud.
en.16:50: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
en.16:51: God has said: “Do not take two gods; He is only One God; so fear only Me.”
en.16:52: To Him belongs everything in the heavens and the earth; and to Him obedience is due always. Do you, then, fear anyone other than God?
en.16:53: Whatever blessing you have is from God. And when harm touches you, it is to Him that you groan.
en.16:54: But when He lifts the harm from you, some of you associate others with their Lord.
en.16:55: To show ingratitude for what We have given them. Enjoy yourselves. You will soon know.
en.16:56: And they allocate, to something they do not know, a share of what We have provided for them. By God, you will be questioned about what you have been inventing.
en.16:57: And they attribute to God daughters—exalted is He—and for themselves what they desire.
en.16:58: And when one of them is given news of a female infant, his face darkens, and he chokes with grief.
en.16:59: He hides from the people because of the bad news given to him. Shall he keep it in humiliation, or bury it in the dust? Evil is the decision they make.
en.16:60: Those who do not believe in the Hereafter set a bad example, while God sets the Highest Example. He is the Mighty, the Wise.
en.16:61: If God were to hold mankind for their injustices, He would not leave upon it a single creature, but He postpones them until an appointed time. Then, when their time arrives, they will not delay it by one hour, nor will they advance it.
en.16:62: And they attribute to God what they themselves dislike, while their tongues utter the lie that theirs is the goodness. Without a doubt, for them is the Fire, and they will be neglected.
en.16:63: By God, We sent messengers to communities before you, but the Adversary made their deeds appear alluring to them. He is their master today, and they will have a painful punishment.
en.16:64: We revealed to you the Scripture only to clarify for them what they differ about, and guidance and mercy for people who believe.
en.16:65: God sends down water from the sky, with which He revives the earth after its death. In this is a sign for people who listen.
en.16:66: And there is a lesson for you in cattle: We give you a drink from their bellies, from between waste and blood, pure milk, refreshing to the drinkers.
en.16:67: And from the fruits of date-palms and grapevines, you derive sugar and wholesome food. In this is a sign for people who understand.
en.16:68: And your Lord inspired the bee: “Set up hives in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they construct.”
en.16:69: Then eat of all the fruits, and go along the pathways of your Lord, with precision. From their bellies emerges a fluid of diverse colors, containing healing for the people. Surely in this is a sign for people who reflect.
en.16:70: God created you; then He takes you away. Some of you will be brought back to the worst age, so that he will no longer know anything, after having acquired knowledge. God is Omniscient and Omnipotent.
en.16:71: God has favored some of you over others in livelihood. Those who are favored would not give their properties to their servants, to the extent of making them partners in it. Will they then renounce God’s blessings?
en.16:72: God has given you mates from among yourselves; and has produced for you, from your mates, children and grandchildren; and has provided you with good things. Will they then believe in falsehood, and refuse God’s favors?
en.16:73: And yet they serve besides God what possesses no provisions for them in the heavens, nor on earth, nor are they capable.
en.16:74: So do not cite the examples for God. God knows, and you do not know.
en.16:75: God cites the example of a bonded slave, who has no power over anything; and someone to whom We have given plentiful provision, from which he gives secretly and openly. Are they equal in comparison? All praise belongs to God, but most of them do not know.
en.16:76: And God cites the example of two men: one of them dumb, unable to do anything, and is a burden on his master; whichever way he directs him, he achieves nothing good. Is he equal to him who commands justice, and is on a straight path?
en.16:77: To God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. The coming of the Hour is only as the twinkling of the eye, or even nearer. God has power over everything.
en.16:78: God brought you out of your mothers’ wombs, not knowing anything; and He gave you the hearing, and the eyesight, and the brains; that you may give thanks.
en.16:79: Have they not seen the birds, flying in the midst of the sky? None sustains them except God. In this are signs for people who believe.
en.16:80: And God has given you in your homes habitats for you, and has provided for you out of the hides of livestock portable homes for you, so you can use them when you travel, and when you camp; and from their wool, and fur, and hair, furnishings and comfort for a while.
en.16:81: And God has made for you shade out of what He has created, and has given you resorts in the mountains, and has given you garments to protect you from the heat, and garments to protect you from your violence. Thus He completes His blessings upon you, so that you may submit.
en.16:82: But if they turn away, your only duty is clear communication.
en.16:83: They recognize God’s blessing, but then deny it, as most of them are ungrateful.
en.16:84: On the Day when We raise up a witness from every community—those who disbelieved will not be permitted, nor will they be excused.
en.16:85: When those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
en.16:86: And when the idolaters see their associates, they will say, “Our Lord, these are our associates whom we used to invoke besides You.” They will strike back at them with the saying, “Surely you are liars.”
en.16:87: On that Day they will offer their submission to God, and what they had invented will abandon them.
en.16:88: Those who disbelieve and obstruct from God’s path—We will add punishment to their punishment, on account of the mischief they used to make.
en.16:89: On the Day when We raise in every community a witness against them, from among them, and bring you as a witness against these. We have revealed to you the Scripture, as an explanation of all things, and guidance, and mercy and good news for those who submit.
en.16:90: God commands justice, and goodness, and generosity towards relatives. And He forbids immorality, and injustice, and oppression. He advises you, so that you may take heed.
en.16:91: Fulfill God’s covenant when you make a covenant, and do not break your oaths after ratifying them. You have made God your guarantor, and God knows what you do.
en.16:92: And do not be like her who unravels her yarn, breaking it into pieces, after she has spun it strongly. Nor use your oaths as means of deception among you, because one community is more prosperous than another. God is testing you thereby. On the Day of Resurrection, He will make clear to you everything you had disputed about.
en.16:93: Had God willed, He would have made you one congregation, but He leaves astray whom He wills, and He guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
en.16:94: And do not use your oaths to deceive one another, so that a foot may not slip after being firm, and you taste misery because you hindered from God’s path, and incur a terrible torment.
en.16:95: And do not exchange God’s covenant for a small price. What is with God is better for you, if you only knew.
en.16:96: What you have runs out, but what is with God remains. We will reward those who are patient according to the best of their deeds.
en.16:97: Whoever works righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will grant him a good life—and We will reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
en.16:98: When you read the Quran, seek refuge with God from the Adversary the outcast.
en.16:99: He has no authority over those who believe and trust in their Lord.
en.16:100: His authority is only over those who follow him, and those who associate others with Him.
en.16:101: When We substitute a verse in place of another verse—and God knows best what He reveals—they say, “You are an impostor.” But most of them do not know.
en.16:102: Say, “The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord, truthfully, in order to stabilize those who believe, and as guidance and good news for those who submit.”
en.16:103: We are well aware that they say, “It is a human being who is teaching him.” But the tongue of him they allude to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.
en.16:104: Those who do not believe in God’s revelations—God will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
en.16:105: It is those who do not believe in God’s revelations who fabricate falsehood. These are the liars.
en.16:106: Whoever renounces faith in God after having believed—except for someone who is compelled, while his heart rests securely in faith—but whoever willingly opens up his heart to disbelief—upon them falls wrath from God, and for them is a tremendous torment.
en.16:107: That is because they have preferred the worldly life to the Hereafter, and because God does not guide the people who refuse.
en.16:108: It is they whom God has sealed their hearts, and their hearing, and their sight. It is they who are the heedless.
en.16:109: There is no doubt that in the Hereafter they will be the losers.
en.16:110: But then your Lord—for those who emigrated after being persecuted, then struggled and persevered—your Lord thereafter is Forgiving and Merciful.
en.16:111: On the Day when every soul will come pleading for itself, and every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and they will not be wronged.
en.16:112: And God cites the example of a town that was secure and peaceful, with its livelihood coming to it abundantly from every direction. But then it turned unappreciative of God’s blessings, so God made it taste the robe of hunger and fear, because of what they used to craft.
en.16:113: A messenger from among them had come to them, but they denounced him, so the punishment seized them in the midst of their wrongdoing.
en.16:114: Eat of the lawful and good things God has provided for you, and be thankful for God’s blessings, if it is Him that you serve.
en.16:115: He has forbidden you carrion, and blood, and the flesh of swine, and anything consecrated to other than God. But if anyone is compelled by necessity, without being deliberate or malicious, then God is Forgiving and Merciful.
en.16:116: And do not say of falsehood asserted by your tongues, “This is lawful, and this is unlawful,” in order to invent lies and attribute them to God. Those who invent lies and attribute them to God will not succeed.
en.16:117: A brief enjoyment—then they will have a painful punishment.
en.16:118: For those who are Jews, We have prohibited what We related to you before. We did not wrong them, but they used to wrong their own selves.
en.16:119: But towards those who do wrongs in ignorance, and then repent afterwards and reform, your Lord thereafter is Forgiving and Merciful.
en.16:120: Abraham was an exemplary leader, devoted to God, a monotheist, and was not of the polytheists.
en.16:121: Thankful for His blessings. He chose him, and guided him to a straight path.
en.16:122: And We gave him goodness in this world, and in the Hereafter he will be among the virtuous.
en.16:123: Then We inspired you: “Follow the religion of Abraham, the Monotheist. He was not an idol-worshiper.”
en.16:124: The Sabbath was decreed only for those who differed about it. Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection regarding their differences.
en.16:125: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good advice, and debate with them in the most dignified manner. Your Lord is aware of those who stray from His path, and He is aware of those who are guided.
en.16:126: If you were to retaliate, retaliate to the same degree as the injury done to you. But if you resort to patience—it is better for the patient.
en.16:127: So be patient. Your patience is solely from God. And do not grieve over them, and do not be stressed by their schemes.
en.16:128: God is with those who are righteous and those who are virtuous.
en.17:1: Glory to Him who journeyed His servant by night, from the Sacred Mosque, to the Farthest Mosque, whose precincts We have blessed, in order to show him of Our wonders. He is the Listener, the Beholder.
en.17:2: And We gave Moses the Scripture, and made it a guide for the Children of Israel: Take none for protector other than Me.
en.17:3: The descendants of those We carried with Noah. He was an appreciative servant.
en.17:4: And We conveyed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture: You will commit evil on earth twice, and you will rise to a great height.
en.17:5: When the first of the two promises came true, We sent against you servants of Ours, possessing great might, and they ransacked your homes. It was a promise fulfilled.
en.17:6: Then We gave you back your turn against them, and supplied you with wealth and children, and made you more numerous.
en.17:7: If you work righteousness, you work righteousness for yourselves; and if you commit evil, you do so against yourselves. Then, when the second promise comes true, they will make your faces filled with sorrow, and enter the Temple as they entered it the first time, and utterly destroy all that falls into their power.
en.17:8: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you. But if you revert, We will revert. We have made the Inferno a prison for the those who deny the truth.
en.17:9: This Quran guides to what is most upright; and it gives good news to the believers who do good deeds, that they will have a great reward.
en.17:10: And those who do not believe in the Hereafter—We have prepared for them a painful punishment.
en.17:11: The human being prays for evil as he prays for good. The human being is very hasty.
en.17:12: We have made the night and the day two wonders. We erased the wonder of the night, and made the wonder of the day revealing, that you may seek bounty from your Lord, and know the number of years, and the calculation. We have explained all things in detail.
en.17:13: For every person We have attached his fate to his neck. And on the Day of Resurrection, We will bring out for him a book which he will find spread open.
en.17:14: “Read your book; today there will be none but yourself to call you to account.”
en.17:15: Whoever is guided—is guided for his own good. And whoever goes astray—goes astray to his detriment. No burdened soul carries the burdens of another, nor do We ever punish until We have sent a messenger.
en.17:16: When We decide to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, they transgress in it, so the word becomes justified against it, and We destroy it completely.
en.17:17: How many generations have We destroyed after Noah? Your Lord is sufficient as Knower and Beholder of the sins of his servants.
en.17:18: Whoever desires the fleeting life, We expedite for him what We decide to give him, to whomever We desire. Then We consign him to the Inferno, where he will roast, condemned and defeated.
en.17:19: But whoever desires the Hereafter, and pursues it as it should be pursued, while he is a believer; these—their effort will be appreciated.
en.17:20: To all—these and those—We extend from the gifts of your Lord. The gifts of your Lord are not restricted.
en.17:21: See how We have favored some of them over others; yet the Hereafter is greater in ranks, and greater in favors.
en.17:22: Do not set up another god with God, lest you become condemned and damned.
en.17:23: Your Lord has commanded that you worship none but Him, and that you be good to your parents. If either of them or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them a word of disrespect, nor scold them, but say to them kind words.
en.17:24: And lower to them the wing of humility, out of mercy, and say, “My Lord, have mercy on them, as they raised me when I was a child.”
en.17:25: Your Lord knows best what is in your minds. If you are righteous—He is Forgiving to the obedient.
en.17:26: And give the relative his rights, and the poor, and the wayfarer, and do not squander wastefully.
en.17:27: The extravagant are brethren of the devils, and the devil is ever ungrateful to his Lord.
en.17:28: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, then say to them words of comfort.
en.17:29: And do not keep your hand tied to your neck, nor spread it out fully, lest you end up liable and regretful.
en.17:30: Your Lord expands the provision for whomever He wills, and restricts it. He is fully Informed, Observant of His servants.
en.17:31: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them, and for you. Killing them is a grave sin.
en.17:32: And do not come near adultery. It is immoral, and an evil way.
en.17:33: And do not kill the soul which God has made sacred, except in the course of justice. If someone is killed unjustly, We have given his next of kin certain authority. But he should not be excessive in killing, for he will be supported.
en.17:34: And do not go near the orphan’s property, except with the best of intentions, until he has reached his maturity. And honor your pledge, because the pledge involves responsibility.
en.17:35: And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with accurate scales. That is fair, and the best determination.
en.17:36: And do not occupy yourself with what you have no knowledge of. The hearing, and the sight, and the brains—all these will be questioned.
en.17:37: And do not walk proudly on earth. You can neither pierce the earth, nor can you match the mountains in height.
en.17:38: The evil of all these is disliked by your Lord.
en.17:39: That is some of the wisdom your Lord has revealed to you. Do not set up with God another god, or else you will be thrown in the Inferno, rebuked and banished.
en.17:40: Has your Lord favored you with sons, while choosing for Himself daughters from among the divine messengers? You are indeed saying a terrible thing.
en.17:41: We have explained in this Quran in various ways, that they may remember, but it only adds to their rebellion.
en.17:42: Say, “If there were other gods with Him, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne.”
en.17:43: Be He glorified. He is exalted, far above what they say.
en.17:44: Praising Him are the seven heavens, and the earth, and everyone in them. There is not a thing that does not glorify Him with praise, but you do not understand their praises. He is indeed Forbearing and Forgiving.
en.17:45: When you read the Quran, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible barrier.
en.17:46: And We drape veils over their hearts, preventing them from understanding it, and heaviness in their ears. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Quran, they turn their backs in aversion.
en.17:47: We know well what they listen to, when they listen to you, as they conspire, when the evildoers say, “You only follow a man bewitched.”
en.17:48: Note what they compared you to. They are lost, and unable to find a way.
en.17:49: And they say, “When we have become bones and fragments, shall we really be resurrected as a new creation?”
en.17:50: Say, “Even if you become rocks or iron.
en.17:51: Or some substance, which, in your minds, is even harder.” Then they will say, “Who will restore us?” Say, “The One who originated you the first time.” Then they will nod their heads at you, and say, “When will it be?” Say, “Perhaps it will be soon.”
en.17:52: On the Day when He calls you, you will respond with His praise, and you will realize that you stayed only a little.
en.17:53: Tell My servants to say what is best. the Adversary sows discord among them. the Adversary is to man an open enemy.
en.17:54: Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy on you; and if He wills, He will punish you. We did not send you as their advocate.
en.17:55: Your Lord knows well everyone in the heavens and the earth. We have given some prophets advantage over others; and to David We gave the Psalms.
en.17:56: Say, “Call upon those you claim besides Him. They have no power to relieve your adversity, nor can they change it.”
en.17:57: Those they call upon are themselves seeking means of access to their Lord, vying to be nearer, and hoping for His mercy, and fearing His punishment. The punishment of your Lord is to be dreaded.
en.17:58: There is no city but We will destroy before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with a severe punishment. This is inscribed in the Scripture.
en.17:59: Nothing prevents Us from sending miraculous signs, except that the ancients called them lies. We gave Thamood the she-camel, a visible sign, but they mistreated her. We do not send the signs except to instill reverence.
en.17:60: We said to you that your Lord encompasses humanity. We did not make the vision We showed you, except as a test for the people, and the tree cursed in the Quran. We frighten them, but that only increases their defiance.
en.17:61: When We said to the divine messengers, “Bow down before Adam,” they bowed down, except for the Adversary. He said, “Shall I bow down before someone You created from mud?”
en.17:62: He said, “Do You see this one whom You have honored more than me? If You reprieve me until the Day of Resurrection, I will bring his descendants under my sway, except for a few.”
en.17:63: He said, “Begone! Whoever of them follows you—the Inferno is your reward, an ample reward.”
en.17:64: “And entice whomever of them you can with your voice, and rally against them your cavalry and your infantry, and share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them.” But the Adversary promises them nothing but delusion.
en.17:65: “As for My devotees, you have no authority over them.” Your Lord is an adequate Guardian.
en.17:66: Your Lord is He who propels for you the ships at sea, that you may seek of His bounty. He is towards you Most Merciful.
en.17:67: When harm afflicts you at sea, those you pray to vanish, except for Him. But when He saves you to land, you turn away. The human being is ever thankless.
en.17:68: Are you confident that He will not cause a track of land to cave in beneath you, or unleash a tornado against you, and then you find no protector?
en.17:69: Or are you confident that He will not return you to it once again, and unleash a hurricane against you, and drown you for your ingratitude? Then you will find no helper against Us.
en.17:70: We have honored the Children of Adam, and carried them on land and sea, and provided them with good things, and greatly favored them over many of those We created.
en.17:71: On the Day when We call every people with their leader. Whoever is given his record in his right hand—these will read their record, and they will not be wronged one bit.
en.17:72: But whoever is blind in this, he will be blind in the Hereafter, and further astray from the way.
en.17:73: They almost lured you away from what We have revealed to you, so that you would invent something else in Our name. In that case, they would have taken you for a friend.
en.17:74: Had We not given you stability, you might have inclined towards them a little.
en.17:75: Then We would have made you taste double in life, and double at death; then you would have found for yourself no helper against Us.
en.17:76: They almost provoked you, to expel you from the land. In that case, they would not have lasted after you, except briefly.
en.17:77: The tradition of the messengers We sent before you—you will find no change in Our rules.
en.17:78: Perform the devotional prayer (Ṣalāh) at the decline of the sun, until the darkness of the night; and the Quran at dawn. The Quran at dawn is witnessed.
en.17:79: And keep vigil with it during parts of the night, as an extra devotional prayer (Ṣalāh). Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a laudable position.
en.17:80: And say, “My Lord, lead me in through an entry of truth, and lead me out through an exit of truth, and grant me from You a supporting power.”
en.17:81: And say, “The truth has come, and falsehood has withered away; for falsehood is bound to wither away.”
en.17:82: We send down in the Quran healing and mercy for the believers, but it increases the evildoers only in loss.
en.17:83: When We bless the human being, he turns away and distances himself. But when adversity touches him, he is in despair.
en.17:84: Say, “Each does according to his disposition. Your Lord knows best who is better guided in the way.”
en.17:85: And they ask you about the Spirit. Say, “The Spirit belongs to the domain of my Lord; and you were given only little knowledge.”
en.17:86: If We willed, We could take away what We revealed to you. Then you will find for yourself no protecting guardian against Us.
en.17:87: Except through a mercy from your Lord. His favors upon you have been great.
en.17:88: Say, “If mankind and jinn came together to produce the like of this Quran, they could never produce the like of it, even if they backed up one another.”
en.17:89: We have displayed for mankind in this Quran every kind of similitude, but most people insist on denying the truth.
en.17:90: And they said, “We will not believe in you unless you make a spring burst from the ground for us.
en.17:91: Or you have a garden of palms and vines; then cause rivers to gush pouring through them.
en.17:92: Or make the sky fall on us in pieces, as you claim, or bring God and the divine messengers before us.
en.17:93: Or you possess a house of gold. Or you ascend into the sky. Even then, we will not believe in your ascension, unless you bring down for us a book that we can read.” Say, “Glory be to my Lord. Am I anything but a human messenger?”
en.17:94: Nothing prevented the people from believing, when guidance has come to them, except that they said, “Did God send a human messenger?”
en.17:95: Say, “If there were angels on earth, walking around in peace, We would have sent down to them from heaven an angel messenger.”
en.17:96: Say, “God is enough witness between you and me. He is fully aware of His servants, and He sees them well.”
en.17:97: Whomever God guides is the guided one. And whomever He leaves astray—for them you will find no protectors apart from Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection, on their faces, blind, dumb, and deaf. Their abode is the Inferno; whenever it abates, We intensify the blaze for them.
en.17:98: This is their repayment for having blasphemed against Our revelations, and having said, “Shall we, when we have become bones and fragments, be resurrected as a new creation?”
en.17:99: Do they not consider that God, Who created the heavens and the earth, is Able to create the likes of them? He has assigned for them a term, in which there is no doubt. But the evildoers persist in denying the truth.
en.17:100: Say, “If you possessed the treasuries of my Lord’s mercy, you would have withheld them for fear of spending.” The human being has always been stingy.
en.17:101: We gave Moses nine clear signs—ask the Children of Israel. When he went to them, Pharaoh said to him, “I think that you, Moses, are bewitched.”
en.17:102: He said, “You know that none sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth—eye openers; and I think that you, Pharaoh, are doomed.”
en.17:103: He resolved to scare them off the land, but We drowned him, and those with him, altogether.
en.17:104: After him, We said to the Children of Israel, “Inhabit the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter arrives, We will bring you all together.”
en.17:105: With the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended. We sent you only as a bearer of good news and a warner.
en.17:106: A Quran which We unfolded gradually, that you may recite to the people over time. And We revealed it in stages.
en.17:107: Say, “Believe in it, or do not believe.” Those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, they fall to their chins, prostrating.
en.17:108: And they say, “Glory to our Lord. The promise of our Lord is fulfilled.”
en.17:109: And they fall to their chins, weeping, and it adds to their humility.
en.17:110: Say, “Call Him God, or call Him the Most Merciful. Whichever name you use, to Him belong the Best Names.” And be neither loud in your devotional prayer (Ṣalāh), nor silent in it, but follow a course in between.
en.17:111: And say, “Praise be to God, who has not begotten a son, nor has He a partner in sovereignty, nor has He an ally out of weakness, and glorify Him constantly.”
en.18:1: Praise be to God, who revealed the Scripture to His servant, and allowed in it no distortion.
en.18:2: Valuable—to warn of severe punishment from Himself; and to deliver good news to the believers who do righteous deeds, that they will have an excellent reward.
en.18:3: In which they will abide forever.
en.18:4: And to warn those who say, “God has begotten a son.”
en.18:5: They have no knowledge of this, nor did their forefathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths. They say nothing but a lie.
en.18:6: Perhaps you may destroy yourself with grief, chasing after them, if they do not believe in this information.
en.18:7: We made what is upon the earth an ornament for it, to test them as to which of them is best in conduct.
en.18:8: And We will turn what is on it into barren waste.
en.18:9: Did you know that the People of the Cave and the Inscription were of Our wondrous signs?
en.18:10: When the youths took shelter in the cave, they said, “Our Lord, give us mercy from Yourself, and bless our affair with guidance.”
en.18:11: Then We sealed their ears in the cave for a number of years.
en.18:12: Then We awakened them to know which of the two groups could better calculate the length of their stay.
en.18:13: We relate to you their story in truth. They were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.
en.18:14: And We strengthened their hearts, when they stood up and said, “Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we will not call on any god besides Him, for then we would have spoken an outrage.”
en.18:15: “These people, our people, have taken to themselves gods other than Him. Why do they not bring a clear proof concerning them? Who, then, does greater wrong than he who invents lies and attributes them to God?”
en.18:16: “Now that you have withdrawn from them, and from what they worship besides God, take shelter in the cave. And your Lord will unfold His mercy for you, and will set your affair towards ease.”
en.18:17: You would have seen the sun, when it rose, veering away from their cave towards the right, and when it sets, moving away from them to the left, as they lay in the midst of the cave. That was one of God’s wonders. He whom God guides is truly guided; but he whom He misguides, for him you will find no directing friend.
en.18:18: You would think them awake, although they were asleep. And We turned them over to the right, and to the left, with their dog stretching its paws across the threshold. Had you looked at them, you would have turned away from them in flight, and been filled with fear of them.
en.18:19: Even so, We awakened them, so that they may ask one another. A speaker among them said, “How long have you stayed?” They said, “We have stayed a day, or part of a day.” They said, “Your Lord knows best how long you have stayed.” “Send one of you to the city, with this money of yours, and let him see which food is most suitable, and let him bring you some provision thereof. And let him be gentle, and let no one become aware of you.”
en.18:20: “If they discover you, they will stone you, or force you back into their religion; then you will never be saved.”
en.18:21: So it was, that We caused them to be discovered, that they would know that the promise of God is true, and that of the Hour there is no doubt. As they were disputing their case among themselves, they said, “Build over them a building.” Their Lord knows best about them. Those who prevailed over their case said, “We will set up over them a place of worship.”
en.18:22: They will say, “Three, and their fourth being their dog.” And they will say, “Five, and their sixth being their dog,” guessing at the unknown. And they will say, “Seven, and their eighth being their dog.” Say, “My Lord knows best their number.” None knows them except a few. So do not argue concerning them except with an obvious argument, and do not consult any of them about them.
en.18:23: And never say about anything, “I will do that tomorrow.”
en.18:24: Without saying, “If God wills.” And remember your Lord if you forget, and say, “Perhaps my Lord will guide me to nearer than this in integrity.”
en.18:25: And they stayed in their cave for three hundred years, adding nine.
en.18:26: Say, “God knows best how long they stayed.” His is the mystery of the heavens and the earth. By Him you see and hear. They have no guardian apart from Him, and He shares His Sovereignty with no one.
en.18:27: And recite what was revealed to you from the Scripture of your Lord. There is no changing His words, and you will find no refuge except in Him.
en.18:28: And content yourself with those who pray to their Lord morning and evening, desiring His Presence. And do not turn your eyes away from them, desiring the glitter of this world. And do not obey him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance—so he follows his own desires—and his priorities are confused.
en.18:29: And say, “The truth is from your Lord. Whoever wills—let him believe. And whoever wills—let him disbelieve”. We have prepared for the unjust a Fire, whose curtains will hem them in. And when they cry for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces. What a miserable drink, and what a terrible place.
en.18:30: As for those who believe and lead a righteous life—We will not waste the reward of those who work righteousness.
en.18:31: These will have the Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow. Reclining on comfortable furnishings, they will be adorned with bracelets of gold, and will wear green garments of silk and brocade. What a wonderful reward, and what an excellent resting-place.
en.18:32: And cite for them the parable of two men. To one of them We gave two gardens of vine, and We surrounded them with palms-trees, and We placed between them crops.
en.18:33: Both gardens produced their harvest in full, and suffered no loss. And We made a river flow through them.
en.18:34: And thus he had abundant fruits. He said to his friend, as he conversed with him, “I am wealthier than you, and greater in manpower.”
en.18:35: And he entered his garden, wronging himself. He said, “I do not think this will ever perish.”
en.18:36: “And I do not think the Hour is coming. And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will find something better than this in return.”
en.18:37: His friend said to him, as he conversed with him, “Are you being ungrateful to Him who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then evolved you into a man?
en.18:38: But as for me, He is God, my Lord, and I never associate with my Lord anyone.
en.18:39: When you entered your garden, why did you not say, “As God wills; there is no power except through God”? Although you see me inferior to you in wealth and children.
en.18:40: Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and release upon it thunderbolts from the sky, so it becomes barren waste.
en.18:41: Or its water will sink into the ground, and you will be unable to draw it.”
en.18:42: And ruin closed in on his crops, and so he began wringing his hands over what he had invested in it, as it lays fallen upon its trellises. And he was saying, “I wish I never associated anyone with my Lord.”
en.18:43: He had no faction to help him besides God, and he was helpless.
en.18:44: That is because authority belongs to God, the True. He is Best in rewarding, and Best in requiting.
en.18:45: And cite for them the parable of the present life: it is like water that We send down from the sky; the plants of the earth absorb it; but then it becomes debris, scattered by the wind. God has absolute power over everything.
en.18:46: Wealth and children are the adornments of the present life. But the things that last, the virtuous deeds, are better with your Lord for reward, and better for hope.
en.18:47: On the Day when We set the mountains in motion; and you see the earth emerging; and We gather them together, and leave none of them behind.
en.18:48: They will be presented before your Lord in a row. “You have come to Us as We created you the first time. Although you claimed We would not set a meeting for you.”
en.18:49: And the book will be placed, and you will see the sinners fearful of its contents. And they will say, “Woe to us! What is with this book that leaves nothing, small or big, but it has enumerated it?” They will find everything they had done present. Your Lord does not wrong anyone.
en.18:50: We said to the divine messengers, “Bow down to Adam.” So they bowed down, except for the Adversary. He was of the jinn, and he defied the command of his Lord. Will you take him and his offspring as lords instead of Me, when they are an enemy to you? Evil is the exchange for the evildoers.
en.18:51: I did not call them to witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation; and I do not take the misleaders for assistants.
en.18:52: On the Day when He will say, “Call on My partners whom you have claimed.” They will call on them, but they will not answer them. And We will place between them a barrier.
en.18:53: And the sinners will see the Fire, and will realize that they will tumble into it. They will find no deliverance from it.
en.18:54: We have elaborated in this Quran for the people every kind of example, but the human being is a most argumentative being.
en.18:55: What prevented people from accepting faith, when guidance has come to them, and from seeking their Lord’s forgiveness? Unless they are waiting for the precedent of the ancients to befall them, or to have the punishment come upon them face to face.
en.18:56: We send the messengers only as deliverers of good news and warners. Those who disbelieve argue with false argument, in order to defeat the truth thereby. They take My Verses, and the warnings, for a joke.
en.18:57: Who does greater wrong than he, who, when reminded of his Lord’s revelations, turns away from them, and forgets what his hands have put forward? We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it, and heaviness in their ears. And if you call them to guidance, they will not be guided, ever.
en.18:58: Your Lord is the Forgiver, Possessor of Mercy. Were He to call them to account for what they have earned, He would have hastened the punishment for them. But they have an appointment from which they will find no escape.
en.18:59: And these towns—We destroyed them when they committed injustices, and We set for their destruction an appointed time.
en.18:60: Recall when Moses said to his servant, “I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two rivers, even if it takes me years.”
en.18:61: Then, when they reached the junction between them, they forgot about their fish. It found its way into the river, slipping away.
en.18:62: When they went further, he said to his servant, “Bring us our lunch; we were exposed in our travel to much fatigue.”
en.18:63: He said, “Do you remember when we rested by the rock? I forgot about the fish. It was only the devil who made me forget it. And so it found its way to the river, amazingly.”
en.18:64: He said, “This is what we were seeking.” And so they turned back retracing their steps.
en.18:65: Then they came upon a servant of Ours, whom We had blessed with mercy from Us, and had taught him knowledge from Our Own.
en.18:66: Moses said to him, “May I follow you, so that you may teach me some of the guidance you were taught?”
en.18:67: He said, “You will not be able to endure with me.
en.18:68: And how will you endure what you have no knowledge of?”
en.18:69: He said, “You will find me, God willing, patient; and I will not disobey you in any order of yours.”
en.18:70: He said, “If you follow me, do not ask me about anything, until I myself make mention of it to you.”
en.18:71: So they set out. Until, when they had boarded the boat, he holed it. He said, “Did you hole it, to drown its passengers? You have done something awful.”
en.18:72: He said, “Did I not tell you that you will not be able to endure with me?”
en.18:73: He said, “Do not rebuke me for forgetting, and do not make my course difficult for me.”
en.18:74: Then they set out. Until, when they encountered a boy, he killed him. He said, “Did you kill a pure soul, who killed no one? You have done something terrible.”
en.18:75: He said, “Did I not tell you that you will not be able to endure with me?”
en.18:76: He said, “If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep company with me. You have received excuses from me.”
en.18:77: So they set out. Until, when they reached the people of a town, they asked them for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. There they found a wall about to collapse, and he repaired it. He said, “If you wanted, you could have obtained a payment for it.”
en.18:78: He said, “This is the parting between you and me. I will tell you the interpretation of what you were unable to endure.
en.18:79: As for the boat, it belonged to paupers working at sea. I wanted to damage it because there was a king coming after them seizing every boat by force.
en.18:80: As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared he would overwhelm them with oppression and disbelief.
en.18:81: So we wanted their Lord to replace him with someone better in purity, and closer to mercy.
en.18:82: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphaned boys in the town. Beneath it was a treasure that belonged to them. Their father was a righteous man. Your Lord wanted them to reach their maturity, and then extract their treasure—as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do it of my own accord. This is the interpretation of what you were unable to endure.”
en.18:83: And they ask you about Zul-Qarnain. Say, “I will tell you something about him.”
en.18:84: We established him on earth, and gave him all kinds of means.
en.18:86: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a murky spring, and found a people in its vicinity. We said, “O Zul-Qarnain, you may either inflict a penalty, or else treat them kindly.”
en.18:87: He said, “As for him who does wrong, we will penalize him, then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with an unheard-of torment.
en.18:88: “But as for him who believes and acts righteously, he will have the finest reward, and We will speak to him of Our command with ease.”
en.18:90: Until, when he reached the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it.
en.18:91: And so it was. We had full knowledge of what he had.
en.18:93: Until, when he reached the point separating the two barriers, he found beside them a people who could barely understand what is said.
en.18:94: They said, “O Zul-Qarnain, the Gog and Magog are spreading chaos in the land. Can we pay you, to build between us and them a wall?”
en.18:95: He said, “What my Lord has empowered me with is better. But assist me with strength, and I will build between you and them a dam.”
en.18:96: “Bring me blocks of iron.” So that, when he had leveled up between the two cliffs, he said, “Blow.” And having turned it into a fire, he said, “Bring me tar to pour over it.”
en.18:97: So they were unable to climb it, and they could not penetrate it.
en.18:98: He said, “This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes true, He will turn it into rubble, and the promise of my Lord is always true.”
en.18:99: On that Day, We will leave them surging upon one another. And the Trumpet will be blown, and We will gather them together.
en.18:100: On that Day, We will present the those who deny the truth to the Inferno, all displayed.
en.18:101: Those whose eyes were screened to My message, and were unable to hear.
en.18:102: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants for masters instead of Me? We have prepared the Inferno for the hospitality of the faithless.
en.18:103: Say, “Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in their works?”
en.18:104: “Those whose efforts in this world are misguided, while they assume that they are doing well.”
en.18:105: It is they who rejected the communications of their Lord, and the encounter with Him. So their works are in vain. And on the Day of Resurrection, We will consider them of no weight.
en.18:106: That is their requital—the Inferno—on account of their disbelief, and their taking My revelations and My messengers in mockery.
en.18:107: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will have the Gardens of the eternal Gardens for hospitality.
en.18:108: Abiding therein forever, without desiring any change therefrom.
en.18:109: Say, “If the ocean were ink for the words of my Lord, the ocean would run out, before the words of my Lord run out,” even if We were to bring the like of it in addition to it.
en.18:110: Say, “I am only a human being like you, being inspired that your god is One God. Whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him work righteousness, and never associate anyone with the service of his Lord.”
en.19:2: A mention of the mercy of your Lord towards His servant Zechariah.
en.19:3: When he called on his Lord, a call in seclusion.
en.19:4: He said, “My Lord, my bones have become feeble, and my hair is aflame with gray, and never, Lord, have I been disappointed in my devotional prayer (Ṣalāh) to you.
en.19:5: “And I fear for my dependents after me, and my wife is barren. So grant me, from Yourself, an heir.
en.19:6: To inherit me, and inherit from the House of Jacob, and make him, my Lord, pleasing.”
en.19:7: “O Zechariah, We give you good news of a son, whose name is John, a name We have never given before.”
en.19:8: He said, “My Lord, how can I have a son, when my wife is barren, and I have become decrepit with old age?”
en.19:9: He said, “It will be so, your Lord says, ‘it is easy for me, and I created you before, when you were nothing.’”
en.19:10: He said, “My Lord, give me a sign.” He said, “Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights straight.”
en.19:11: And he came out to his people, from the sanctuary, and signaled to them to praise morning and evening.
en.19:12: “O John, hold on to the Scripture firmly,” and We gave him wisdom in his youth.
en.19:13: And tenderness from Us, and innocence. He was devout.
en.19:14: And kind to his parents; and he was not a disobedient tyrant.
en.19:15: And peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the Day he is raised alive.
en.19:16: And mention in the Scripture Mary, when she withdrew from her people to an eastern location.
en.19:17: She screened herself away from them, and We sent to her Our spirit, and He appeared to her as an immaculate human.
en.19:18: She said, “I take refuge from you in the Most Merciful, should you be righteous.”
