en.20:94: He said, “Son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or my head. I feared you would say, `You have caused division among the Children of Israel, and did not regard my word.'“
en.20:95: He said, “What do you have to say, O Samarian?”
en.20:96: He said, “I saw what they did not see, so I grasped a handful from the Envoy’s traces, and I flung it away. Thus my soul prompted me.”
en.20:97: He said, “Begone! Your lot in this life is to say, ‘No contact.’ And you have an appointment that you will not miss. Now look at your god that you remained devoted to—we will burn it up, and then blow it away into the sea, as powder.”
en.20:98: Surely your god is God, the One besides whom there is no other god. He comprehends everything in knowledge.
en.20:99: Thus We narrate to you reports of times gone by; and We have given you a message from Our Presence.
en.20:100: Whoever turns away from it will carry on the Day of Resurrection a burden.
en.20:101: Abiding therein forever. And wretched is their burden on the Day of Resurrection.
en.20:102: On the Day when the Trumpet is blown—We will gather the sinners on that Day, blue.
en.20:103: Murmuring among themselves: “You have lingered only for ten.”
en.20:104: We are fully aware of what they say, when the most exemplary of them in conduct will say, “You have lingered only a day.”
en.20:105: And they ask you about the mountains. Say, “My Lord will crumble them utterly.”
en.20:107: You will see in them neither crookedness, nor deviation.”
en.20:108: On that Day, they will follow the caller, without any deviation. Voices will be hushed before the Merciful, and you will hear nothing but murmur.
en.20:109: On that Day, intercession will not avail, except for him permitted by the Merciful, and whose words He has approved.
en.20:110: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot comprehend Him in their knowledge.
en.20:111: Faces will be humbled before the Living, the Eternal. Whoever carries injustice will despair.
en.20:112: But whoever has done righteous deeds, while being a believer—will fear neither injustice, nor grievance.
en.20:113: Thus We have revealed it an Arabic Quran, and We have diversified the warnings in it, that perhaps they would become righteous, or it may produce a lesson for them.
en.20:114: Exalted is God, the True King. Do not be hasty with the Quran before its inspiration to you is concluded, and say, “My Lord, increase me in knowledge.”
en.20:115: And We covenanted with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no resolve.
en.20:116: And when We said to the divine messengers, “Bow down to Adam.” They bowed down, except for the Adversary; he refused.
en.20:117: We said, “O Adam, this is an enemy to you and to your wife. So do not let him make you leave the Garden of Paradise, for then you will suffer.
en.20:118: In it you will never go hungry, nor be naked.
en.20:119: Nor will you be thirsty in it, nor will you swelter.”
en.20:120: But the Adversary whispered to him. He said, “O Adam, shall I show you the Tree of Immortality, and a kingdom that never decays?”
en.20:121: And so they ate from it; whereupon their bodies became visible to them, and they started covering themselves with the leaves of the Garden of Paradise. Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord, and fell.
en.20:122: But then his Lord recalled him, and pardoned him, and guided him.
en.20:123: He said, “Go down from it, altogether; some of you enemies of some others. But whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance, will not go astray, nor suffer.
en.20:124: But whoever turns away from My Reminder, for him is a confined life. And We will raise him on the Day of Resurrection blind.”
en.20:125: He will say, “My Lord, why did You raise me blind, though I was seeing?”
en.20:126: He will say, “Just as Our revelations came to you, and you forgot them, today you will be forgotten.”
en.20:127: Thus We recompense him who transgresses and does not believe in the revelations of his Lord. The punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, and more lasting.
en.20:128: Is it not instructive to them, how many generations before them We destroyed, in whose settlements they walk? Surely in that are signs for people of understanding.
en.20:129: Were it not for a word that issued from your Lord, the inevitable would have happened, but there is an appointed term.
en.20:130: So bear patiently what they say, and celebrate the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun, and before its setting. And during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the borders of the day, that you may be satisfied.
en.20:131: And do not extend your glance towards what We have given some classes of them to enjoy—the splendor of the life of this world—that We may test them thereby. Your Lord’s provision is better, and more lasting.
en.20:132: And exhort your people to pray, and patiently adhere to it. We ask of you no sustenance, but it is We who sustain you. The good ending is that for righteousness.
en.20:133: And they say, “Why does he not bring us a miracle from his Lord?” Were they not given enough miracles in the former scriptures?
en.20:134: Had We destroyed them with a punishment before him, they would have said, “Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger, we would have followed Your revelations before we were humiliated and disgraced.”
en.20:135: Say, “Everybody is waiting, so wait. You will know who the people of the straight path are, and who is rightly-guided.
en.21:1: Mankind’s reckoning has drawn near, but they turn away heedlessly.
en.21:2: No fresh reminder comes to them from their Lord, but they listen to it playfully.
en.21:3: Their hearts distracted, the evildoers confer secretly, “Is this anything but a mortal like you? Will you take to sorcery, with open-eyes?”
en.21:4: He said, “My Lord knows what is said in the heaven and the earth; and He is the Hearer, the Knower.”
en.21:5: And they said, “A jumble of dreams,” and, “He made it up,” and, “He is a poet,” “let him bring us a sign, like those sent to the ancients.”
en.21:6: None of the towns We destroyed before them had believed. Will they, then, believe?
en.21:7: We did not send before you except men, whom We inspired. Ask the people of knowledge, if you do not know.
en.21:8: We did not make them mere bodies that ate no food, nor were they immortal.
en.21:9: Then We fulfilled Our promise to them, and We saved them together with whomever We willed, and We destroyed the extravagant.
en.21:10: We have sent down to you a Book, containing your message. Do you not understand?
en.21:11: How many a guilty town have We crushed, and established thereafter another people?
en.21:12: Then, when they sensed Our might, they started running away from it.
en.21:13: Do not run, but come back to your luxuries, and to your homes, that you may be questioned.
en.21:14: They said, “Woe to us; we were unfair.”
en.21:15: This continued to be their cry, until We made them silent ashes.
en.21:16: We did not create the sky and the earth and what is between them for amusement.
en.21:17: If We wanted amusement, We could have found it within Us, were We to do so.
en.21:18: In fact, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, so it vanishes. Woe unto you, for what you describe.
en.21:19: To Him belongs everyone in the heavens and the earth. Those near Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they waver.
en.21:20: They praise night and day, without ever tiring.
en.21:21: Or have they taken to themselves gods from the earth who resurrect?
en.21:22: If there were in them gods other than God, they would have gone to ruin. So glory be to God, Lord of the Throne, beyond what they allege.
en.21:23: He will not be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
en.21:24: Or have they taken, besides Him, other gods? Say, “Bring your proof. This is a message for those with me, and a message of those before me.” But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.
en.21:25: We never sent a messenger before you without inspiring him that: “There is no god but I, so worship Me.”
en.21:26: And they say, “The Most Merciful has taken to himself a son.” Be He glorified; they are but honored servants.
en.21:27: They never speak before He has spoken, and they only act on His command.
en.21:28: He knows what is before them, and what is behind them; and they do not intercede except for him whom He approves; and they tremble in awe of Him.
en.21:29: And whoever of them says, “I am a god besides Him,” We will reward him with the Inferno. Thus We reward the evildoers.
en.21:30: Do the those who deny the truth not see that the heavens and the earth were one mass, and We tore them apart? And We made from water every living thing. Will they not believe?
en.21:31: And We placed on earth stabilizers, lest it sways with them, and We placed therein signposts and passages, that they may be guided.
en.21:32: And We made the sky a protected ceiling; yet they turn away from its wonders.
en.21:33: It is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each floating in an orbit.
en.21:34: We did not grant immortality to any human being before you. Should you die, are they then the immortal?
en.21:35: Every soul will taste death. We burden you with adversity and prosperity—a test. And to Us you will be returned.
en.21:36: When those who disbelieve see you, they treat you only with ridicule: “Is this the one who mentions your gods?” And they reject the mention of the Merciful.
en.21:37: The human being was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not seek to rush Me.
en.21:38: And they say, “When will this promise come true, if you are truthful?”
en.21:39: If those who disbelieve only knew, when they cannot keep the fire off their faces and off their backs, and they will not be helped.
en.21:40: In fact, it will come upon them suddenly, and bewilder them. They will not be able to repel it, and they will not be reprieved.
en.21:41: Messengers before you were also ridiculed, but those who jeered were surrounded by what they had ridiculed.
en.21:42: Say, “Who guards you against the Merciful by night and by day?” But they turn away from the mention of their Lord.
en.21:43: Or do they have gods who can defend them against Us? They cannot help themselves, nor will they be protected from Us.
en.21:44: We have given these enjoyments, and their ancestors, until time grew long upon them. Do they not see how We gradually reduce the land from its extremities? Are they then the victors?
en.21:45: Say, “I am warning you through inspiration.” But the deaf cannot hear the call when they are being warned.
en.21:46: And when a breath of your Lord’s punishment touches them, they say, “Woe to us, we were truly wicked.”
en.21:47: We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul will suffer the least injustice. And even if it be the weight of a mustard-seed, We will bring it up. Sufficient are We as Reckoners.
en.21:48: We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion, and illumination, and a reminder for the virtuous.
en.21:49: Those who fear their Lord in private, and are apprehensive of the Hour.
en.21:50: This too is a blessed message that We revealed. Are you going to deny it?
en.21:51: We gave Abraham his integrity formerly, and We knew him well.
en.21:52: When he said to his father and his people, “What are these statues to which you are devoted?”
en.21:53: They said, “We found our parents worshiping them.”
en.21:54: He said, “You and your parents are in evident error.”
en.21:55: They said, “Are you telling us the truth, or are you just playing?”
en.21:56: He said, “Your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the One who created them, and I bear witness to that.
en.21:57: “By God, I will have a plan for your statues after you have gone away.”
en.21:58: So he reduced them into pieces, except for their biggest, that they may return to it.
en.21:59: They said, “Who did this to our gods? He is certainly one of the evildoers.”
en.21:60: They said, “We heard a youth mentioning them. He is called Abraham.”
en.21:61: They said, “Bring him before the eyes of the people, so that they may witness.”
en.21:62: They said, “Are you the one who did this to our gods, O Abraham?”
en.21:63: He said, “But it was this biggest of them that did it. Ask them, if they can speak.”
en.21:64: Then they turned to one another, and said, “You yourselves are the evildoers.”
en.21:65: But they reverted to their old ideas: “You certainly know that these do not speak.”
en.21:66: He said, “Do you worship, instead of God, what can neither benefit you in anything, nor harm you?
en.21:67: Fie on you, and on what you worship instead of God. Do you not understand?”
en.21:68: They said, “Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act.”
en.21:69: We said, “O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.”
en.21:70: They planned to harm him, but We made them the worst losers.
en.21:71: And We delivered him, and Lot, to the land that We blessed for all people.
en.21:72: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob as a gift; and each We made righteous.
en.21:73: And We made them leaders, guiding by Our command; and We inspired them to do good works, and to observe the devotional prayer (Ṣalāh), and to give out charity. They were devoted servants to Us.
en.21:74: And Lot—We gave him judgment and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that practiced the abominations. They were wicked and perverted people.
en.21:75: And We admitted him into Our mercy; for He was one of the virtuous.
en.21:76: And Noah, when he called before. So We answered him, and delivered him and his family from the great disaster.
en.21:77: And We supported him against the people who rejected Our signs. They were an evil people, so We drowned them all.
en.21:78: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment in the case of the field, when some people’s sheep wandered therein by night; and We were witnesses to their judgment.
en.21:79: And so We made Solomon understand it, and to each We gave wisdom and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains along with David to sing Our praises, and the birds as well—surely We did.
en.21:80: And We taught him the making of shields for you, to protect you from your violence. Are you, then, appreciative?
en.21:81: And to Solomon the stormy wind, blowing at His command towards the land that We have blessed. We are aware of everything.
en.21:82: And of the devils were some that dived for him, and performed other, lesser tasks. But We kept them restrained.
en.21:83: And Job, when he cried out to his Lord: “Great harm has afflicted me, and you are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
en.21:84: So We answered him, lifted his suffering, and restored his family to him, and their like with them—a mercy from Us, and a reminder for the worshipers.
en.21:85: And Ishmael, and Enoch, and Ezekiel; each was one of the steadfast.
en.21:86: And We admitted them into Our mercy. They were among the virtuous.
en.21:87: And Jonah, when he stormed out in fury, thinking We had no power over him. But then He cried out in the darkness, “There is no god but You! Glory to You! I was one of the evildoers!”
en.21:88: So We answered him, and saved him from the affliction. Thus We save the faithful.
en.21:89: And Zechariah, when he called out to his Lord, “My Lord, do not leave me alone, even though you are the Best of heirs.”
en.21:90: So We answered him, and gave him John. And We cured his wife for him. They used to vie in doing righteous deeds, and used to call on Us in love and awe, and they used to humble themselves to Us.
en.21:91: And she who guarded her virginity. We breathed into her of Our spirit, and made her and her son a sign to the world.
en.21:92: This community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
en.21:93: But they splintered themselves into factions. They will all return to Us.
en.21:94: Whoever does righteous deeds, and is a believer, his effort will not be denied. We are writing it down for him.
en.21:95: There is a ban on the town that We had destroyed—that they will not return.
en.21:96: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swarm down from every mound.
en.21:97: The promise of truth has drawn near. The eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror: “Woe to us. We were oblivious to this. In fact, we were evildoers.”
en.21:98: You and what you worship besides God are fuel for the Inferno. You will descend into it.
en.21:99: Had these been gods, they would not have descended into it. All will abide in it.
en.21:100: In it they will wail. In it they will not hear.
en.21:101: As for those who deserved goodness from Us—these will be kept away from it.
en.21:102: They will not hear its hissing, and they will forever abide in what their hearts desire.
en.21:103: The Supreme Fear will not worry them, and the divine messengers will receive them: “This is your Day which you were promised.”
en.21:104: On the Day when We fold the heaven, like the folding of a book. Just as We began the first creation, We will repeat it—a promise binding on Us. We will act.
en.21:105: We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.
en.21:106: Indeed, in this is a message for people who worship.
en.21:107: We did not send you except as mercy to mankind.
en.21:108: Say, “It is revealed to me that your God is One God. Are you going to submit?”
en.21:109: But if they turn away, say, “I have informed you sufficiently. Although I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far.”
en.21:110: He knows what is said openly, and He knows what you conceal.
en.21:111: “And I do not know whether it is perhaps a trial for you, and an enjoyment for a while.”
en.21:112: He said, “My Lord, judge with justice.” And, “Our Lord is the Gracious, Whose help is sought against what you allege.”
en.22:1: O people, be conscious of your Lord. The quaking of the Hour is a tremendous thing.
en.22:2: On the Day when you will see it: every nursing mother will discard her infant, and every pregnant woman will abort her load, and you will see the people drunk, even though they are not drunk—but the punishment of God is severe.
en.22:3: Among the people is he who argues about God without knowledge, and follows every defiant devil.
en.22:4: It was decreed for him, that whoever follows him—he will misguide him, and lead him to the torment of the Blaze.
en.22:5: O people! If you are in doubt about the Resurrection—We created you from dust, then from a small drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, partly developed and partly undeveloped. In order to clarify things for you. And We settle in the wombs whatever We will for a designated term, and then We bring you out as infants, until you reach your full strength. And some of you will pass away, and some of you will be returned to the vilest age, so that he may not know, after having known. And you see the earth still; but when We send down water on it, it vibrates, and swells, and grows all kinds of lovely pairs.
en.22:6: That is because God is the truth, and because He gives life to the dead, and because He is Capable of everything.
en.22:7: And because the Hour is coming—there is no doubt about it—and because God will resurrect those in the graves.
en.22:8: And among the people is he who argues about God without knowledge, or guidance, or an enlightening scripture.
en.22:9: Turning aside in contempt, to lead away from the path of God. He will have humiliation in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection We will make him taste the agony of burning.
en.22:10: That is for what your hands have advanced, and because God is not unjust to the servants.
en.22:11: And among the people is he who worships God on edge. When something good comes his way, he is content with it. But when an ordeal strikes him, he makes a turnaround. He loses this world and the next. That is the obvious loss.
en.22:12: He invokes, instead of God, what can neither harm him nor benefit him. That is the far straying.
en.22:13: He invokes one whose harm is closer than his benefit. What a miserable master. What a miserable companion.
en.22:14: God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into Gardens beneath which rivers flow. God does whatever He wills.
en.22:15: Whoever thinks that God will not help him in this life and in the Hereafter—let him turn to heaven, then sever, and see if his cunning eliminates what enrages him.
en.22:16: Thus We revealed it as clarifying signs, and God guides whomever He wills.
en.22:17: Those who believe, and those who are Jewish, and the Sabeans, and the Christians, and the Zoroastrians, and the Polytheists—God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. God is witness to all things.
en.22:18: Do you not realize that to God prostrates everyone in the heavens and everyone on earth, and the sun, and the moon, and the stars, and the mountains, and the trees, and the animals, and many of the people? But many are justly deserving of punishment. Whomever God shames, there is none to honor him. God does whatever He wills.
en.22:19: Here are two adversaries feuding regarding their Lord. As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be tailored for them, and scalding water will be poured over their heads.
en.22:20: Melting their insides and their skins.
en.22:21: And they will have maces of iron.
en.22:22: Whenever they try to escape the gloom, they will be driven back to it: “Taste the suffering of burning.”
en.22:23: But God will admit those who believe and do good deeds into Gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be decorated therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be of silk.
en.22:24: They were guided to purity of speech. They were guided to the path of the Most Praised.
en.22:25: As for those who disbelieve and repel from God’s path and from the Sacred Mosque—which We have designated for all mankind equally, whether residing therein or passing through—and seek to commit sacrilege therein—We will make him taste of a painful punishment.
en.22:26: We showed Abraham the location of the House: “Do not associate anything with Me; and purify My House for those who circle around, and those who stand to pray, and those who kneel and prostrate.”
en.22:27: And announce the the sacred pilgrimage (Ḥajj) to humanity. They will come to you on foot, and on every transport. They will come from every distant point.
en.22:28: That they may witness the benefits for themselves, and celebrate the name of God during the appointed days, for providing them with the animal livestock. So eat from it, and feed the unfortunate poor.
en.22:29: Then let them perform their acts of cleansing, and fulfill their vows, and circle around the Ancient House.
en.22:30: All that. Whoever venerates the sanctities of God—it is good for him with his Lord. All livestock are permitted to you, except what is recited to you. So stay away from the abomination of idols, and stay away from perjury.
en.22:31: Being true to God, without associating anything with Him. Whoever associates anything with God—it is as though he has fallen from the sky, and is snatched by the birds, or is swept away by the wind to a distant abyss.
en.22:32: So it is. Whoever venerates the sacraments of God—it is from the piety of the hearts.
en.22:33: In them are benefits for you until a certain time. Then their place is by the Ancient House.
en.22:34: We have appointed a rite for every nation, that they may commemorate God’s name over the livestock He has provided for them. Your God is One God, so to Him submit, and announce good news to the humble.
en.22:35: Those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned, and those who endure what has befallen them, and those who perform the devotional prayer (Ṣalāh) and spend from what We have provided for them.
en.22:36: We have made the animal offerings emblems of God for you. In them is goodness for you. So pronounce God’s name upon them as they line up. Then, when they have fallen on their sides, eat of them and feed the contented and the beggar. Thus We have subjected them to you, that you may be thankful.
en.22:37: Neither their flesh, nor their blood, ever reaches God. What reaches Him is the righteousness from you. Thus He subdued them to you, that you may glorify God for guiding you. And give good news to the charitable.
en.22:38: God defends those who believe. God does not love any ungrateful traitor.
en.22:39: Permission is given to those who are fought against, and God is Able to give them victory.
en.22:40: Those who were unjustly evicted from their homes, merely for saying, “Our Lord is God.” Were it not that God repels people by means of others: monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques—where the name of God is mentioned much—would have been demolished. God supports whoever supports Him. God is Strong and Mighty.
en.22:41: Those who, when We empower them in the land, observe the devotional prayer (Ṣalāh), and give regular charity, and command what is right, and forbid what is wrong. To God belongs the outcome of events.
en.22:42: If they deny you—before them the people of Noah, and Aad, and Thamood also denied.
en.22:43: And the people of Abraham, and the people of Lot.
en.22:44: And the inhabitants of Median. And Moses was denied. Then I reprieved those who disbelieved, but then I seized them. So how was My rejection?
en.22:45: How many a town have We destroyed while it was doing wrong? They lie in ruins; with stilled wells, and lofty mansions.
en.22:46: Have they not journeyed in the land, and had minds to reason with, or ears to listen with? It is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts, within the chests, that go blind.
en.22:47: And they ask you to hasten the punishment. But God never breaks His promise. A day with your Lord is like a thousand years of your count.
en.22:48: How many a town have I reprieved, although it was unjust? Then I seized it. To Me is the destination.
en.22:49: Say, “O people, I am only a plain warner to you.”
en.22:50: Those who believe and work righteousness—for them is forgiveness and a generous provision.
en.22:51: But those who strive against Our revelations—these are the inmates of the Inferno.
en.22:52: We never sent a messenger before you, or a messenger of God, but when he had a desire the Adversary interfered in his wishes. But God nullifies what the Adversary interjects, and God affirms His revelations. God is Omniscient and Wise.
en.22:53: In order to make the Adversary’s suggestions a trial for those whose hearts are diseased, and those whose hearts are hardened. The evildoers are in profound discord.
en.22:54: And so that those endowed with knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, and so believe in it, and their hearts soften to it. God guides those who believe to a straight path.
en.22:55: Those who disbelieve will continue to be hesitant about it, until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or there comes to them the torment of a desolate Day.
en.22:56: Sovereignty on that Day belongs to God; He will judge between them. Those who believe and do good deeds will be in the Gardens of Bliss.
en.22:57: But those who disbelieve and reject Our revelations—these will have a humiliating punishment.
en.22:58: Those who emigrate in God’s cause, then get killed, or die, God will provide them with fine provisions. God is the Best of Providers.
en.22:59: He will admit them an admittance that will please them. God is Knowing and Clement.
en.22:60: That is so! Whoever retaliates similarly to the affliction he was made to suffer, and then he is wronged again, God will definitely assist him. God is Pardoning and Forgiving.
en.22:61: That is because God merges the night into the day, and He merges the day into the night, and because God is Hearing and Seeing.
en.22:62: That is because God is the Reality, and what they invoke besides Him is vanity, and because God is the Sublime, the Grand.
en.22:63: Do you not see that God sends down water from the sky, and the land becomes green? God is Kind and Aware.
en.22:64: To Him belongs everything in the heavens and everything on earth. God is the Rich, the Praised.
en.22:65: Do you not see that God made everything on earth subservient to you? How the ships sail at sea by His command? That He holds up the sky lest it falls on earth—except by His permission? God is Gracious towards the people, Most Merciful.
en.22:66: And it is He who gives you life, then makes you die, then revives you. The human being is unappreciative.
en.22:67: For every congregation We have appointed acts of devotion, which they observe. So do not let them dispute with you in this matter. And invite to your Lord; you are upon a straight guidance.
en.22:68: But if they dispute with you, say, “God is fully aware of what you do.”
en.22:69: God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection regarding what you disagree about.
en.22:70: Do you not know that God knows everything in the heavens and the earth? This is in a book. That is easy for God.
en.22:71: Yet they worship, besides God, things for which He sent down no warrant, and what they have no knowledge of. There is no savior for the transgressors.
en.22:72: And when Our Clear Verses are recited to them, you will recognize disgust on the faces of those who disbelieve. They nearly assault those who recite to them Our Verses. Say, “Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire! God has promised it to those who disbelieve. And what a wretched outcome!”
en.22:73: O people! A parable is presented, so listen to it: Those you invoke besides God will never create a fly, even if they banded together for that purpose. And if the fly steals anything from them, they cannot recover it from it. Weak are the pursuer and the pursued.
en.22:74: They do not value God as He should be valued. God is Strong and Powerful.
en.22:75: God chooses messengers from among the divine messengers, and from among the people. God is Hearing and Seeing.
en.22:76: He knows what is before them, and what is behind them. To God all matters are referred.
en.22:77: O you who believe! Kneel, and prostrate, and worship your Lord, and do good deeds, so that you may succeed.
en.22:78: And strive for God, with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you, and has not burdened you in religion—the faith of your father Abraham. It is he who named you Muslims before, and in this. So that the Envoy may be a witness over you, and you may be witnesses over the people. So pray regularly, and give regular charity, and cleave to God. He is your Protector. What an excellent Protector, and what an excellent Helper.
en.23:2: Those who are humble in their prayers.
en.23:6: Except from their spouses, or their dependents—for then they are free from blame.
en.23:7: But whoever seeks anything beyond that—these are the transgressors.
en.23:8: Those who are faithful to their trusts and pledges.
en.23:11: Who will inherit the eternal Gardens, wherein they will dwell forever.
en.23:12: We created man from an extract of clay.
en.23:13: Then We made him a seed, in a secure repository.
en.23:14: Then We developed the seed into a clot. Then We developed the clot into a lump. Then We developed the lump into bones. Then We clothed the bones with flesh. Then We produced it into another creature. Most Blessed is God, the Best of Creators.
en.23:15: Then, after that, you will die.
en.23:16: Then, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be resurrected.
en.23:17: We created above you seven pathways, and We are never heedless of the creation.
en.23:18: And We sent down water from the sky in proper quantity, and settled it in the ground, and We are Able to take it away.
en.23:19: With it We produce for you gardens of palms and vines, yielding abundant fruit for you to eat.
en.23:20: And a tree springing out of Mount Sinai, producing oil, and seasoning for those who eat.
en.23:21: And there is a lesson for you in livestock: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, and you have many benefits in them, and from them you eat.
en.23:22: And on them, and on the ships, you are transported.
en.23:23: We sent Noah to his people. He said, “O my people, worship God, you have no deity other than Him. Will you not take heed?”
en.23:24: But the notables of his people, who disbelieved, said, “This is nothing but a human like you, who wants to gain superiority over you. Had God willed, He would have sent down angels. We never heard of this from our forefathers of old.
en.23:25: He is nothing but a man possessed. Just ignore him for a while.”
en.23:26: He said, “My Lord, help me, for they have rejected me.”
en.23:27: So We inspired him: “Build the Ark under Our observation and by Our inspiration. And when Our decree comes to pass, and the oven boils over, load into it two pairs of every kind, together with your family, except those of them against whom the word has already been pronounced. And do not speak to me concerning those who did wrong; for they are to be drowned.”
en.23:28: Then, when you and those with you are settled in the Ark, say, “Praise be to God, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people.”
en.23:29: And say, “My Lord, land me with a blessed landing, as you are the best of transporters.”
en.23:30: Surely in that are signs. We are always testing.
en.23:31: Then, after them, We established another generation.
en.23:32: And We sent among them a messenger from themselves: “Serve God. You have no god other than Him. Will you not be cautious?”
en.23:33: But the dignitaries of his people, those who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and We had indulged them in the present life, said, “This is nothing but a human like you; he eats what you eat, and he drinks what you drink.
en.23:34: If you obey a human being like yourselves, then you will be losers.
en.23:35: Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought out?
en.23:36: Farfetched, farfetched is what you are promised.
en.23:37: There is nothing but our life in this world. We die, and we live, and we are not resurrected.
en.23:38: He is nothing but a man, making up lies about God. We have no faith in him.”
en.23:39: He said, “My Lord, help me, for they have rejected me.”
en.23:40: He said, “Soon they will be filled with regret.”
en.23:41: Then the Blast struck them, justifiably, and We turned them into scum. So away with the wicked people.
en.23:42: Then, after them, We raised other generations.
en.23:43: No nation can advance its time, nor can they postpone it.
en.23:44: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time a messenger came to his community, they called him a liar. So We made them follow one another, and made them history. So away with a people who do not believe.
en.23:45: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron, with Our signs and a clear authority.
en.23:46: To Pharaoh and his nobles, but they turned arrogant. They were oppressive people.
en.23:47: They said, “Are we to believe in two mortals like us, and their people are our slaves?”
en.23:48: So they called them liars, and thus were among those destroyed.
en.23:49: And We gave Moses the Scripture, that they may be guided.
en.23:50: And We made Mary’s son and his mother a sign, and We sheltered them on high ground with security and flowing springs.
en.23:51: O messengers, eat of the good things, and act with integrity. I am aware of what you do.
en.23:52: This nation of yours is one nation, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.
en.23:53: But they tore themselves into sects; each party happy with what they have.
en.23:54: So leave them in their bewilderment until a time.
en.23:55: Do they assume that, in furnishing them with wealth and children.
en.23:56: We race to give them the good things? In fact, they have no idea.
en.23:57: Those who, from awe of their Lord, are fearful.
en.23:58: And those who believe in their Lord’s Verses.
en.23:59: And those who associate no partners with their Lord.
en.23:60: And those who give what they give, while their hearts quake, knowing that to their Lord they will return.
en.23:61: It is they who race towards goodness. It is they who will reach it first.
en.23:62: We never burden any soul beyond its capacity. And with Us is a record that tells the truth, and they will not be wronged.
en.23:63: But their hearts are puzzled because of this; and they have deeds that do not conform to this, which they continue to perpetrate.
en.23:64: Until, when We seize the decadent among them with torment, they begin to groan.
en.23:65: Do not groan today. You will receive no help from Us.
en.23:66: My Verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels.
en.23:67: Arrogant towards it—talked nonsense about it—disregarded it.
en.23:68: Have they not pondered the Word? Or has there come to them what came not to their forefathers of old?
en.23:69: Or is it that they did not recognize their messenger, so they are denying him?
en.23:70: Or do they say, “He is possessed?” In fact, he brought them the truth, but most of them hate the truth.
en.23:71: If the truth conformed to their desires, the heavens, the earth, and everyone in them would have gone to ruin. In fact, We have given them their message, but they keep avoiding their message.
en.23:72: Or are you asking them for a payment? The revenue from your Lord is better, and He is the Best of providers.
en.23:73: You are inviting them to a straight path.
en.23:74: But those who do not believe in the Hereafter are swerving from the path.
en.23:75: Even if We had mercy on them, and relieved their problems, they would still blindly persist in their defiance.
en.23:76: We have already gripped them with suffering, but they did not surrender to their Lord, nor did they humble themselves.
en.23:77: Until, when We have opened before them a gate of intense agony, at once they will despair.
en.23:78: It is He who produced for you the hearing, and the eyesight, and the feelings. But little gratitude you show.
en.23:79: And it is He who multiplied you on earth, and to Him you will be gathered.
en.23:80: And it is He who gives life and brings death, and to Him is the alternation of night and day. Do you not understand?
en.23:81: But they say the like of what the ancients said.
en.23:82: They say, “After we have died, and become dust and bones, will we be resurrected?
en.23:83: We were promised this before—we and our ancestors—these are nothing but legends of the ancients.”
en.23:84: Say, “To whom does the earth belong, and everyone in it, if you happen to know?”
en.23:85: They will say, “To God.” Say, “Will you not reflect?”
en.23:86: Say, “Who is the Lord of the seven heavens, and Lord of the Splendid Throne?”
en.23:87: They will say, “To God.” Say, “Will you not become righteous?”
en.23:88: Say, “In whose hand is the dominion of all things, and He protects and cannot be protected from, if you happen to know?”
en.23:89: They will say, “To God.” Say, “Then are you bewitched?”
en.23:90: In fact, We have given them the truth, and they are liars.
en.23:91: God has never begotten a son, nor is there any god besides Him. Otherwise, each god would have taken away what it has created, and some of them would have gained supremacy over others. Glory be to God, far beyond what they describe.
en.23:92: The Knower of the hidden and the manifest. He is exalted, far above what they associate.
en.23:93: Say, “My Lord, if You would show me what they are promised.
en.23:94: My Lord, do not place me among the wicked people.”
en.23:95: We are surely Able to show you what We promise them.
en.23:96: Repel evil by what is better. We are aware of what they describe.
en.23:97: And say, “My Lord, I seek refuge with You from the urgings of the devils.
en.23:98: And I seek refuge with You, my Lord, lest they become present.”
en.23:99: Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, “My Lord, send me back.
en.23:100: That I may do right in what I have neglected.” By no means! It is just a word that he utters. And behind them is a barrier, until the Day they are resurrected.
en.23:101: When the Horn is blown, no relations between them will exist on that Day, and they will not ask after one another.
en.23:102: Those whose scales are heavy—those are the successful.
en.23:103: But those whose scales are light—those are they who have lost their souls; in the Inferno they will dwell forever.
en.23:104: The Fire lashes their faces, and therein they grimace.
en.23:105: “Were not My revelations recited to you, and you kept on rejecting them?”
en.23:106: They will say, “Our Lord, our wretchedness prevailed over us, and we were a people astray.
en.23:107: Our Lord! Bring us out of this. If we ever returned, we would truly be evil.”
en.23:108: He will say, “Be despised therein, and do not speak to Me.
en.23:109: There was a group of My servants who would say, `Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us, and have mercy on us; You are the Best of the merciful.'
en.23:110: But you made then a target of ridicule, until they made you forget My remembrance; and you used to laugh at them.
en.23:111: Today, I have rewarded them for their endurance. They are the ones who are the triumphant.”
en.23:112: He will say, “How many years did you remain on earth?”
en.23:113: They will say, “We remained a day, or part of a day; but ask those who keep count.”
en.23:114: He will say, “You remained only for a little while, if you only knew.
en.23:115: Did you think that We created you in vain, and that to Us you will not be returned?”
en.23:116: So Exalted is God, the Ruler, the Real. There is no god except He, the Lord of the Noble Throne.
en.23:117: Whoever invokes another god besides God—he has no proof thereof—his reckoning rests with his Lord. The those who deny the truth will not succeed.
en.23:118: And say, “My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the Best of the merciful.”
en.24:1: A chapter that We have revealed, and made obligatory, and revealed in it clear Verses, that you may take heed.
en.24:2: The adulteress and the adulterer—whip each one of them a hundred lashes, and let no pity towards them overcome you regarding God’s Law, if you believe in God and the Last Day. And let a group of believers witness their punishment.
en.24:3: The adulterer shall marry none but an adulteress or an idolatress; and the adulteress shall marry none but an adulterer or an idolater. That has been prohibited for the believers.
en.24:4: Those who accuse chaste women, then cannot bring four witnesses, whip them eighty lashes, and do not ever accept their testimony. For these are the immoral.
en.24:5: Except for those who repent afterwards, and reform; for God is Forgiving and Merciful.
en.24:6: As for those who accuse their own spouses, but have no witnesses except themselves, the testimony of one of them is equivalent to four testimonies, if he swears by God that he is truthful.
en.24:7: And the fifth time, that God’s curse be upon him, if he is a liar.
en.24:8: But punishment shall be averted from her, if she swears four times by God, that he is a liar.
en.24:9: And the fifth time, that God’s wrath be upon her, if he is truthful.
en.24:10: Were it not for God’s grace upon you, and His mercy, and that God is Conciliatory and Wise.
en.24:11: Those who perpetrated the slander are a band of you. Do not consider it bad for you, but it is good for you. Each person among them bears his share in the sin. As for him who played the major role—for him is a terrible punishment.
en.24:12: Why, when you heard about it, the believing men and women did not think well of one another, and say, “This is an obvious lie”?
en.24:13: Why did they not bring four witnesses to testify to it? If they fail to bring the witnesses, then in God’s sight, they are liars.
en.24:14: Were it not for God’s favor upon you, and His mercy, in this world and the Hereafter, you would have suffered a great punishment for what you have ventured into.
en.24:15: When you rumored it with your tongues, and spoke with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you considered it trivial; but according to God, it is serious.
en.24:16: When you heard it, you should have said, “It is not for us to repeat this. By Your glory, this is a serious slander.”
en.24:17: God cautions you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers.
en.24:18: God explains the Verses to you. God is Knowing and Wise.
en.24:19: Those who love to see immorality spread among the believers—for them is a painful punishment, in this life and in the Hereafter. God knows, and you do not know.
en.24:20: Were it not for God’s grace upon you, and His mercy, and that God is Clement and Merciful.
en.24:21: O you who believe! Do not follow the Adversary’s footsteps. Whoever follows the Adversary’s footsteps—he advocates obscenity and immorality. Were it not for God’s grace towards you, and His mercy, not one of you would have been pure, ever. But God purifies whomever He wills. God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
en.24:22: Those of you who have affluence and means should not refuse to give to the relatives, and the needy, and the emigrants for the sake of God. And let them pardon, and let them overlook. Do you not love for God to pardon you? God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
en.24:23: Those who slander honorable, innocent, believing women are cursed in this life and in the Hereafter. They will have a terrible punishment.
en.24:24: On the Day when their tongues, and their hands, and their feet will testify against them regarding what they used to do.
en.24:25: On that Day, God will pay them their account in full, and they will know that God is the Evident Reality.
en.24:26: Bad women are for bad men, and bad men are for bad women, and good women are for good men, and good men are for good women. Those are acquitted of what they say. There is forgiveness for them, and a generous provision.
en.24:27: O you who believe! Do not enter homes other than your own, until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants. That is better for you, that you may be aware.
en.24:28: And if you find no one in them, do not enter them until you are given permission. And if it is said to you, “Turn back,” then turn back. That is more proper for you. God is aware of what you do.
en.24:29: There is no blame on you for entering uninhabited houses, in which are belongings of yours. God knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
en.24:30: Tell the believing men to restrain their looks, and to guard their privates. That is purer for them. God is cognizant of what they do.
en.24:31: And tell the believing women to restrain their looks, and to guard their privates, and not display their beauty except what is apparent thereof, and to draw their coverings over their breasts, and not expose their beauty except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, what their right hands possess, their male attendants who have no sexual desires, or children who are not yet aware of the nakedness of women. And they should not strike their feet to draw attention to their hidden beauty. And repent to God, all of you believers, so that you may succeed.
en.24:32: And wed the singles among you, and those who are fit among your servants and maids. If they are poor, God will enrich them from His bounty. God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
en.24:33: And let those who do not find the means to marry abstain, until God enriches them from His bounty. If any of your servants wish to be freed, grant them their wish, if you recognize some good in them. And give them of God’s wealth which he has given you. And do not compel your girls to prostitution, seeking the materials of this life, if they desire to remain chaste. Should anyone compel them—after their compulsion, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
en.24:34: We have sent down to you clarifying revelations, and examples of those who passed on before you, and advice for the virtuous.
en.24:35: God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The allegory of His light is that of a pillar on which is a lamp. The lamp is within a glass. The glass is like a brilliant planet, fueled by a blessed tree, an olive tree, neither eastern nor western. Its oil would almost illuminate, even if no fire has touched it. Light upon Light. God guides to His light whomever He wills. God thus cites the parables for the people. God is cognizant of everything.
en.24:36: In houses which God has permitted to be raised, and His name is celebrated therein. He is glorified therein, morning and evening.
en.24:37: By men who neither trading nor commerce distracts them from God’s remembrance, and from performing the prayers, and from giving alms. They fear a Day when hearts and sights are overturned.
en.24:38: God will reward them according to the best of what they did, and He will increase them from His bounty. God provides for whomever He wills without reckoning.
en.24:39: As for those who disbelieve, their works are like a mirage in a desert. The thirsty assumes it is to be water. Until, when he has reached it, he finds it to be nothing, but there he finds God, Who settles his account in full. God is swift in reckoning.
en.24:40: Or like utter darkness in a vast ocean, covered by waves, above which are waves, above which is fog. Darkness upon darkness. If he brings out his hand, he will hardly see it. He to whom God has not granted a light has no light.
en.24:41: Do you not realize that God is glorified by whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and even by the birds in formation? Each knows its devotional prayer (Ṣalāh) and its manner of praise. God knows well what they do.
en.24:42: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to God is the ultimate return.
en.24:43: Have you not seen how God propels the clouds, then brings them together, then piles them into a heap, and you see rain drops emerging from its midst? How He brings down loads of hail from the sky, striking with it whomever He wills, and diverting it from whomever He wills? The flash of its lightening almost snatches the sight away.
en.24:44: God alternates the night and the day. In that is a lesson for those who have insight.
en.24:45: God created every living creature from water. Some of them crawl on their bellies, and some walk on two feet, and others walk on four. God creates whatever He wills. God is Capable of everything.
en.24:46: We sent down enlightening revelations, and God guides whomever He wills to a straight path.
en.24:47: And they say, “We have believed in God and the Envoy, and we obey,” but some of them turn away afterwards. These are not believers.
en.24:48: And when they are called to God and His Envoy, in order to judge between them, some of them refuse.
en.24:49: But if justice is on their side, they accept it willingly.
en.24:50: Is there sickness in their hearts? Or are they suspicious? Or do they fear that God may do them injustice? Or His Envoy? In fact, they themselves are the unjust.
en.24:51: The response of the believers, when they are called to God and His Envoy in order to judge between them, is to say, “We hear and we obey.” These are the successful.
en.24:52: Whoever obeys God and His Envoy, and fears God, and is conscious of Him—these are the winners.
en.24:53: And they swear by God with their solemn oaths, that if you commanded them, they would mobilize. Say, “Do not swear. Obedience will be recognized. God is experienced with what you do.”
en.24:54: Say, “Obey God and obey the Envoy.” But if they turn away, then he is responsible for his obligations, and you are responsible for your obligations. And if you obey him, you will be guided. It is only incumbent on the Envoy to deliver the Clarifying Message.
en.24:55: God has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds, that He will make them successors on earth, as He made those before them successors, and He will establish for them their religion—which He has approved for them—and He will substitute security in place of their fear. They worship Me, never associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that—these are the sinners.
en.24:56: Pray regularly, and give regular charity, and obey the Envoy, so that you may receive mercy.
en.24:57: Never think that those who disbelieve can escape on earth. Their place is the Fire; a miserable destination.
en.24:58: O you who believe! Permission must be requested by your servants and those of you who have not reached puberty. On three occasions: before the Dawn Prayer, and at noon when you change your clothes, and after the Evening Prayer. These are three occasions of privacy for you. At other times, it is not wrong for you or them to intermingle with one another. God thus clarifies the revelations for you. God is Knowledgeable and Wise.
en.24:59: When the children among you reach puberty, they must ask permission, as those before them asked permission. God thus clarifies His revelations for you. God is Knowledgeable and Wise.
en.24:60: Women past the age of childbearing, who have no desire for marriage, commit no wrong by taking off their outer clothing, provided they do not flaunt their finery. But to maintain modesty is better for them. God is Hearing and Knowing.
en.24:61: There is no blame on the blind, nor any blame on the lame, nor any blame on the sick, nor on yourselves for eating at your homes, or your fathers’ homes, or your mothers’ homes, or your brothers’ homes, or your sisters’ homes, or the homes of your paternal uncles, or the homes of your paternal aunts, or the homes of your maternal uncles, or the homes of your maternal aunts, or those whose keys you own, or the homes of your friends. You commit no wrong by eating together or separately. But when you enter any home, greet one another with a greeting from God, blessed and good. God thus explains the revelations for you, so that you may understand.
en.24:62: The believers are those who believe in God and His Envoy, and when they are with him for a matter of common interest, they do not leave until they have asked him for permission. Those who ask your permission are those who believe in God and His Envoy. So when they ask your permission to attend to some affair of theirs, give permission to any of them you wish, and ask God’s forgiveness for them. God is Forgiving and Merciful.
en.24:63: Do not address the Envoy in the same manner you address one another. God knows those of you who slip away using flimsy excuses. So let those who oppose his orders beware, lest an ordeal strikes them, or a painful punishment befalls them.
en.24:64: Surely, to God belongs everything in the heavens and the earth. He knows what you are about. And on the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. God has full knowledge of all things.
en.25:1: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, to be a warning to humanity.
en.25:2: He to whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, who took to Himself no son, who never had a partner in His kingship; who created everything and determined its measure.
en.25:3: And yet, instead of Him, they produce for themselves gods that create nothing, but are themselves created; that have no power to harm or benefit themselves; and no power over life, death, or resurrection.
en.25:4: Those who disbelieve say, “This is nothing but a lie that he made up, and others have helped him at it.” They have committed an injustice and a perjury.
en.25:5: And they say, “Tales of the ancients; he wrote them down; they are dictated to him morning and evening.”
en.25:6: Say, “It was revealed by He who knows the Secret in the heavens and the earth. He is always Forgiving and Merciful.”
en.25:7: And they say, “What sort of messenger is this, who eats food, and walks in the marketplaces? If only an angel was sent down with him, to be alongside him a warner.”
en.25:8: Or, “If only a treasure was dropped on him.” Or, “If only he had a garden from which he eats.” The evildoers also say, “You are following but a man under spell.”
en.25:9: Look how they invent examples for you. They have gone astray, and cannot find a way.
en.25:10: Blessed is He who, if He wills, can provide you with better than that—gardens beneath which rivers flow—and He will give you palaces.
en.25:11: In fact, they have denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a Blaze.
en.25:12: When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear it raging and roaring.
en.25:13: And when they are thrown into it, into a tight place, shackled, they will plead there for death.
en.25:14: “Do not plead for one death today, but plead for a great many deaths.”
en.25:15: Say, “Is this better, or the Garden of Paradise of Eternity promised to the virtuous? It is for them a reward and a destination.
en.25:16: They will have therein whatever they desire, forever. That is upon your Lord a binding promise.
en.25:17: On the Day when He gathers them, and what they worshiped besides God, He will say, “Was it you who misled these servants of Mine, or was it they who lost the way?”
en.25:18: They will say, “Glory be to You. It was not for us to take any lords besides You. But you gave them enjoyments, and their ancestors, until they forgot the Message, and became ruined people.”
en.25:19: They have denied you because of what you say; so you can neither avert, nor help. Whoever among you commits injustice, We will make him taste a grievous punishment.
en.25:20: We never sent any messengers before you, but they ate food and walked in the marketplaces. And We made some of you tempters for one another—will you be patient? Your Lord is always Observing.
en.25:21: Those who do not expect to meet Us say, “If only the divine messengers were sent down to us, or we could see our Lord.” They have grown arrogant within themselves, and have become excessively defiant.
en.25:22: On the Day when they see the divine messengers—there will be no good news for sinners on that Day; and they will say, “A protective refuge.”
en.25:23: We will proceed to the works they did, and will turn them into scattered dust.
en.25:24: The companions of the eternal Gardens on that Day will be better lodged, and more fairly accommodated.
en.25:25: The Day when the sky is cleft with clouds, and the divine messengers are sent down in streams.
en.25:26: On that Day, true sovereignty will belong to the Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the those who deny the truth.
en.25:27: On that Day, the wrongdoer will bite his hands, and say, “If only I had followed the way with the Envoy.
en.25:28: Oh, woe to me; I wish I never took so-and-so for a friend.
en.25:29: He led me away from the Message after it had come to me; for the Adversary has always been a betrayer of man.”
en.25:30: And the Envoy will say, “My Lord, my people have abandoned this Quran.”
en.25:31: Likewise, to every messenger of God We assign enemies from among the wicked. But your Lord suffices as a Guide and Savior.
en.25:32: Those who disbelieve say, “Why was the Quran not revealed to him at once?” Thus in order to strengthen your heart thereby, and We revealed it in stages.
en.25:33: Whatever argument they come to you with, We provide you with the truth, and a better exposition.
en.25:34: Those who are herded into the Inferno on their faces—those are in a worse position, and further astray from the way.
en.25:35: We gave Moses the Scripture, and appointed his brother Aaron as his assistant.
en.25:36: We said, “Go to the people who rejected Our signs,” and We destroyed them completely.
en.25:37: And the people of Noah: when they rejected the messengers, We drowned them, and made them a lesson for mankind. We have prepared for the evildoers a painful retribution.
en.25:38: And Aad, and Thamood, and the inhabitants of Arras, and many generations in between.
en.25:39: To each We presented the parables; and each We devastated utterly.
en.25:40: And they came upon the city that was drenched by the terrible rain. Did they not see it? But they do not expect resurrection.
en.25:41: And when they see you, they take you for nothing but mockery: “Is this the one God sent as a messenger?”
en.25:42: “He nearly led us away from our gods, had we not patiently adhered to them.” But they will know, when they witness the torment, who is further away from the way.
en.25:43: Have you seen him who chose his desire as his god? Would you be an agent for him?
en.25:44: Or do you assume that most of them hear or understand? They are just like cattle, but even more errant in their way.
en.25:45: Do you not see how your Lord extends the shadow? Had He willed, He could have made it still. And We made the sun a pointer to it.
en.25:46: Then We withdraw it towards Us gradually.
en.25:47: And it is He who made the night a covering for you, and sleep for rest; and He made the day a revival.
en.25:48: And it is He who sends the winds, bringing advance news of His mercy; and We send down from the sky pure water.
en.25:49: To revive dead lands thereby, and to provide drink for the multitude of animals and humans We created.
en.25:50: We have circulated it among them, that they may reflect, but most people persist in thanklessness.
en.25:51: Had We willed, We could have sent to every town a warner.
en.25:52: So do not obey the those who deny the truth, but strive against them with it, a mighty struggle.
en.25:53: And it is He who merged the two seas; this one fresh and sweet, and that one salty and bitter; and He placed between them a barrier, and an impassable boundary.
en.25:54: And it is He who, from fluid, created the human being. Then He made relationships through marriage and mating. Your Lord is Omnipotent.
en.25:55: And yet, instead of God, they serve what neither profits them nor harms them. The disbeliever has always turned his back on his Lord.
en.25:56: We sent you only as a herald of good news and a warner.
en.25:57: Say, “I ask of you no payment for this—only that whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.”
en.25:58: And put your trust in the Living, the One who never dies; and celebrate His praise. He suffices as the All-Informed Knower of the faults of His creatures.
en.25:59: He who created the heavens and the earth and everything between them in six days, then settled on the Throne. The Most Merciful. Ask about Him a well-informed.
en.25:60: And when it is said to them, “Bow down to the Merciful,” they say, “And what is the Merciful? Are we to bow down to whatever you command us?” And it increases their aversion.
en.25:61: Blessed is He who placed constellations in the sky, and placed in it a lamp, and an illuminating moon.
en.25:62: And it is He who made the night and the day alternate—for whoever desires to reflect, or desires to show gratitude.
en.25:63: The servants of the Merciful are those who walk the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, “Peace.”
en.25:64: And those who pass the night prostrating themselves to their Lord and standing up.
en.25:65: And those who say, ‘‘Our Lord, avert from us the suffering of the Inferno, for its suffering is continuous.
en.25:66: It is indeed a miserable residence and destination.”
en.25:67: And those who, when they spend, are neither wasteful nor stingy, but choose a middle course between that.
en.25:68: And those who do not implore besides God any other god, and do not kill the soul which God has made sacred—except in the pursuit of justice—and do not commit adultery. Whoever does that will face penalties.
en.25:69: The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will dwell therein in humiliation forever.
en.25:70: Except for those who repent, and believe, and do good deeds. These—God will replace their bad deeds with good deeds. God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
en.25:71: Whoever repents and acts righteously—has inclined towards God with repentance.
en.25:72: And those who do not bear false witness; and when they come across indecencies, they pass by with dignity.
en.25:73: And those who, when reminded of the revelations of their Lord, do not fall before them deaf and blind.
en.25:74: And those who say, “Our Lord, grant us delight in our spouses and our children, and make us a good example for the virtuous.”
en.25:75: Those will be awarded the Chamber for their patience, and will be greeted therein with greetings and peace.
en.25:76: Abiding therein forever—it is an excellent residence and destination.
en.25:77: Say, “What are you to my Lord without your prayers? You have denied the truth, and the inevitable will happen.”
en.26:2: These are the Verses of the Clarifying Book.
en.26:3: Perhaps you will destroy yourself with grief, because they do not become believers.
en.26:4: If We will, We can send down upon them a sign from heaven, at which their necks will stay bent in humility.
en.26:5: No fresh reminder comes to them from the Most Merciful, but they turn their backs at it.
en.26:6: They have denied the truth, but soon will come to them the news of what they ridiculed.
en.26:7: Have they not seen the earth, and how many beautiful pairs We produced therein?
en.26:8: Surely in this is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
en.26:9: Most surely, your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:10: Your Lord called to Moses, “Go to the tyrannical people.
en.26:11: The people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear?”
en.26:12: He said, “My Lord, I fear they will reject me.
en.26:13: And I become stressed, and my tongue is not fluent, so send Aaron too.
en.26:14: And they have a charge against me, so I fear they will kill me.”
en.26:15: He said, “No. Go, both of you, with Our proofs. We will be with you, listening.
en.26:16: Go to Pharaoh, and say, ‘We are the Messengers of the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:17: Let the Children of Israel go with us.'“
en.26:18: He said, “Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed among us for many of your years?
en.26:19: And you committed that deed you committed, and you were ungrateful.”
en.26:20: He said, “I did it then, when I was of those astray.
en.26:21: And I fled from you when I feared you; but my Lord gave me wisdom, and made me one of the messengers.
en.26:22: Is that the favor you taunt me with, although you have enslaved the Children of Israel?”
en.26:23: Pharaoh said, “And what is the Lord of the Worlds?”
en.26:24: He said, “The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and everything between them, if you are aware.”
en.26:25: He said to those around him, “Do you not hear?”
en.26:26: He said, “Your Lord and the Lord of your ancestors of old.”
en.26:27: He said, “This messenger of yours, who is sent to you, is crazy.”
en.26:28: He said, “Lord of the East and the West, and everything between them, if you understand.”
en.26:29: He said, “If you accept any god other than me, I will make you a prisoner.”
en.26:30: He said, “What if I bring you something convincing?”
en.26:31: He said, “Bring it, if you are being truthful.”
en.26:32: So he cast his staff; and it was a serpent, plain to see.
en.26:33: And he pulled his hand; and it was white, for all to see.
en.26:34: He said to the dignitaries around him, “This is a skilled magician.
en.26:35: He intends to drive you out of your land with his magic, so what do you recommend?”
en.26:36: They said, “Delay him and his brother, and send recruiters to the cities.
en.26:37: To bring you every experienced magician.”
en.26:38: So the magicians were gathered for the appointment on a specified day.
en.26:39: And it was said to the people, “Are you all gathered?
en.26:40: That we may follow the magicians, if they are the winners.”
en.26:41: When the magicians arrived, they said to Pharaoh, “Is there a reward for us, if we are the winners?”
en.26:42: He said, “Yes, and you will be among those favored.”
en.26:43: Moses said to them, “Present what you intend to present.”
en.26:44: So they threw their ropes and their sticks, and said, “By the majesty of Pharaoh, we will be the winners.”
en.26:45: Then Moses threw his staff, and behold, it began swallowing their trickery.
en.26:46: And the magicians fell down prostrating.
en.26:47: They said, “We have believed in the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:48: The Lord of Moses and Aaron.”
en.26:49: He said, “Did you believe in Him before I have given you permission? He must be your chief, who taught you magic. You will soon know. I will cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all.”
en.26:50: They said, “No problem. To our Lord we will return.
en.26:51: We are eager for our Lord to forgive us our sins, since we are the first of the believers.”
en.26:52: And We inspired Moses: “Travel with My servants by night. You will be followed.”
en.26:53: Pharaoh sent heralds to the cities.
en.26:56: But we are a vigilant multitude.”
en.26:57: So We drove them out of gardens and springs.
en.26:59: So it was. And We made the Children of Israel inherit them.
en.26:60: And they pursued them at sunrise.
en.26:61: When the two groups sighted each other, the followers of Moses said, “We are being overtaken.”
en.26:62: He said, “No; my Lord is with me, He will guide me.”
en.26:63: We inspired Moses: “Strike the sea with your staff.” Whereupon it parted, and each part was like a huge hill.
en.26:64: And there We brought the others near.
en.26:65: And We saved Moses and those with him, all together.
en.26:67: In that there is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
en.26:68: Surely, your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:69: And relate to them the story of Abraham.
en.26:70: When he said to his father and his people, “What do you worship?”
en.26:71: They said, “We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them.”
en.26:72: He said, “Do they hear you when you pray?
en.26:73: Or do they benefit you, or harm you?”
en.26:74: They said, “But we found our ancestors doing so.”
en.26:75: He said, “Have you considered what you worship.
en.26:77: They are enemies to me, but not so the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:78: He who created me, and guides me.
en.26:79: He who feeds me, and waters me.
en.26:80: And when I get sick, He heals me.
en.26:81: He who makes me die, and then revives me.
en.26:82: He who, I hope, will forgive my sins on the Day of the Reckoning.”
en.26:83: “My Lord! Grant me wisdom, and include me with the virtuous.
en.26:84: And give me a reputation of truth among the others.
en.26:85: And make me of the inheritors of the Garden of Paradise of Bliss.
en.26:86: And forgive my father—he was one of the misguided.
en.26:87: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected.
en.26:88: The Day when neither wealth nor children will help.
en.26:89: Except for him who comes to God with a sound heart.”
en.26:90: And the eternal Gardens will be brought near for the virtuous.
en.26:91: And the Blaze will be displayed to the deviators.
en.26:92: And it will be said to them, “Where are those you used to worship?”
en.26:93: Besides God? Can they help you, or help themselves?”
en.26:94: Then they will be toppled into it, together with the seducers.
en.26:95: And the soldiers of the Adversary, all of them.
en.26:96: They will say, as they feud in it.
en.26:97: “By God, We were in evident error.
en.26:98: For equating you with the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:99: No one misled us except the sinners.
en.26:102: If only we could have another chance, we would be among the faithful.”
en.26:103: Surely in this is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
en.26:104: Your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:105: The people of Noah disbelieved the messengers.
en.26:106: Their brother Noah said to them, “Do you not fear?
en.26:107: I am to you a faithful messenger.
en.26:108: So fear God, and obey me.
en.26:109: I ask of you no payment for this. My payment is only from the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:110: So fear God, and obey me.”
en.26:111: They said, “Shall we believe in you, when it is the lowliest who follow you?”
en.26:112: He said, “What do I know about what they do?
en.26:113: Their account rests only with my Lord, if you have sense.
en.26:114: And I am not about to drive away the believers.
en.26:115: I am only a clear warner.”
en.26:116: They said, “If you do not refrain, O Noah, you will be stoned.”
en.26:117: He said, “My Lord, my people have denied me.
en.26:118: So judge between me and them decisively, and deliver me and the believers who are with me.
en.26:119: So We delivered him and those with him in the laden Ark.
en.26:121: In that is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
en.26:122: Your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:124: When their brother Hud said to them, “Do you not fear?
en.26:125: I am to you a faithful messenger.
en.26:126: So fear God, and obey me.
en.26:127: I ask of you no payment for this. My payment is only from the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:128: Do you build a monument on every height for vanity's sake?
en.26:129: And you set up fortresses, hoping to live forever?
en.26:130: And when you strike, you strike mercilessly?
en.26:131: So fear God, and obey me.
en.26:132: And reverence Him, who supplied you with everything you know.
en.26:133: He supplied you with livestock and children.
en.26:135: I fear for you the punishment of an awesome Day.”
en.26:136: They said, “It is the same for us, whether you lecture us, or do not lecture.
en.26:137: This is nothing but morals of the ancients.
en.26:138: And we will not be punished.”
en.26:139: So they denied him, and We destroyed them. Surely in this is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
en.26:140: Your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:142: When their brother Saleh said to them, “Do you not fear?
en.26:143: I am to you a faithful messenger.
en.26:144: So fear God, and obey me.
en.26:145: I ask of you no payment for it. My payment is only from the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:146: Will you be left secure in what is here?
en.26:148: And fields, and palm-trees whose fruits are delicious?
en.26:149: And you skillfully carve houses in the mountains?
en.26:150: So fear God, and obey me.
en.26:151: And do not obey the command of the extravagant.
en.26:152: Who spread turmoil on earth, and do not reform.”
en.26:153: They said, “You are surely one of the bewitched.
en.26:154: You are nothing but a man like us. So bring us a sign, if you are truthful.
en.26:155: He said, “This is a she-camel; she has her turn of drinking, and you have your turn of drinking—on a specified day.
en.26:156: And do not touch her with harm, lest the punishment of a great day seizes you.”
en.26:157: But they slaughtered her, and became full of remorse.
en.26:158: So the punishment overtook them. Surely in this is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
en.26:159: Your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:160: The people of Lot disbelieved the messengers.
en.26:161: When their brother Lot said to them, “Do you not fear?
en.26:162: I am to you a faithful messenger.
en.26:163: So fear God, and obey me.
en.26:164: I ask of you no payment for it. My payment is only from the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:165: Do you approach the males of the world?
en.26:166: And forsake the wives your Lord created for you? Indeed, you are intrusive people.”
en.26:167: They said, “Unless you refrain, O Lot, you will be expelled.”
en.26:168: He said, “I certainly deplore your conduct.”
en.26:169: “My Lord, save me and my family from what they do.”
en.26:170: So We saved him and his family, altogether.
en.26:171: Except for an old woman among those who tarried.
en.26:173: And We rained down on them a rain. Dreadful is the rain of those forewarned.
en.26:174: Surely in this is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
en.26:175: Your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:176: The People of the Woods disbelieved the messengers.
en.26:177: When Shuaib said to them, “Do you not fear?
en.26:178: I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
en.26:179: So fear God, and obey me.
en.26:180: I ask of you no payment for it. My payment is only from the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:181: Give full measure, and do not cheat.
en.26:183: And do not defraud people of their belongings, and do not work corruption in the land.
en.26:184: And fear Him who created you and the masses of old.”
en.26:185: They said, “You are one of those bewitched.
en.26:186: And you are nothing but a man like us; and we think that you are a liar.
en.26:187: So bring down on us pieces from the sky, if you are truthful.”
en.26:188: He said, “My Lord is Well Aware of what you do.”
en.26:189: But they denied him. So the punishment of the day of gloom gripped them. It was the punishment of a great day.
en.26:190: Surely in this is a sign, but most of them are not believers.
en.26:191: Your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:192: It is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds.
en.26:193: The Honest Spirit came down with it.
en.26:194: Upon your heart, that you may be one of the warners.
en.26:196: And it is in the scriptures of the ancients.
en.26:197: Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel recognized it?
en.26:198: Had We revealed it to one of the foreigners.
en.26:199: And he had recited it to them, they still would not have believed in it.
en.26:200: Thus We make it pass through the hearts of the guilty.
en.26:201: They will not believe in it until they witness the painful punishment.
en.26:202: It will come to them suddenly, while they are unaware.
en.26:203: Then they will say, “Are we given any respite?”
en.26:204: Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?
en.26:205: Have you considered: if We let them enjoy themselves for some years.
en.26:206: Then there comes to them what they were promised.
en.26:207: Of what avail to them will be their past enjoyments?
en.26:208: Never did We destroy a town, but it had warners.
en.26:209: As a reminder—We are never unjust.
en.26:210: It was not the devils that revealed it.
en.26:211: It is not in their interests, nor in their power.
en.26:213: So do not pray to another god with God, else you will be of those tormented.
en.26:215: And lower your wing to those of the believers who follow you.
en.26:216: And if they disobey you, say, “I am innocent of what you do.”
en.26:217: And put your trust in the Almighty, the Merciful.
en.26:218: He Who sees you when you rise.
en.26:219: And your devotions amidst the worshipers.
en.26:220: He is indeed the Hearer, the Aware.
en.26:221: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?
en.26:222: They descend upon every sinful liar.
en.26:223: They give ear, and most of them are liars.
en.26:224: And as for the poets—the deviators follow them.
en.26:225: Do you not see how they ramble in every style?
en.26:226: And how they say what they do not do?
en.26:227: Except for those who believe, and do good deeds, and remember God frequently, and defend themselves after they are wronged. As for those who do wrong, they will know by what overturning they will be overturned.
en.27:1: Ta, Seen. These are the Signs of the Quran—a book that makes things clear.
en.27:2: Guidance and good news for the believers.
en.27:3: Those who observe the prayers, and give charity regularly, and are certain of the Hereafter.
en.27:4: As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter: We made their deeds appear good to them, so they wander aimlessly.
en.27:5: It is they who will receive the grievous punishment—and in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers.
en.27:6: You are receiving the Quran from an All-Wise, All-Knowing.
en.27:7: When Moses said to his family, “I have glimpsed a fire. I will bring you some news from it; or bring you a firebrand, that you may warm yourselves.”
